docs.title: NetPulse
docs.text:
NetPulse is a networking solution for Unity games. It has two parts: a .NET 10 server that you host yourself, and a Unity package (com.netpulse.unity) that works with Unity 2021.3 through 6000.x. The model will be familiar if you have used Photon PUN: players connect, sit in a lobby, create or join rooms, share room and player properties, call RPCs and synchronize networked objects.

Both parts are at version 0.4.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
On the server:

  • Lobby and matchmaking: named rooms, random join with property filters, a live room list with deltas.
  • Rooms that run on their own async fiber, so one slow room never delays the others, the lobby or the network thread.
  • An event cache that replays state to late joiners, and player and empty-room time to live for rejoining.
  • Server-side validation of network object ownership, so a client cannot move, destroy or steal objects it does not own.
  • Flood protection per peer, an AppId and protocol version check, and optional custom authentication.
  • Plugins written in C#: hooks for joins, events, property changes and room closing, timers, HTTP calls, background work and hot reload.
  • Metrics through System.Diagnostics.Metrics and a small set of console commands.

In Unity:

  • An async API (await Pulse.Connect(), await Pulse.JoinOrCreateRoom(...)) with callback and coroutine alternatives.
  • RPCs, SyncVar<T>, typed messages and typed room and player keys, backed by a source generator and analyzers.
  • Network objects with ownership, scene objects, network scenes, a network tick and an offline mode.
  • Editor tools: a settings asset, a Hub window with a traffic profiler, and IL2CPP link.xml generation.

docs.title: How it compares to PUN
docs.text: The concepts map closely, so most PUN code translates by renaming. The main differences are where the server runs and who enforces the rules. NetPulse is self-hosted: you run the server binary on your own machine and write server logic as plugins in C#, instead of relying on a hosted service. The server checks ownership itself, and the Unity API is built around async/await and generated code instead of string-based calls. The page Migrating from PUN lists the concrete replacements.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
If you want to Read Run the server and join a room in a few minutes Getting started Understand rooms, peers, objects and ownership Concepts Write the client side Unity client Run, configure and deploy the server Server Add server-side logic Plugins Write your own client or look up a code Reference Move an existing PUN project Migrating from PUN Fix a problem Troubleshooting and Operations See what changed Changelog

The source for both parts lives on GitHub. The repository is private for now, so you need access to it to clone the server or install the Unity package from git.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: Changes to the server, the plugin SDK and the shared protocol library (NetPulse.Common). The Unity package keeps its own list: see the Unity package changelog. A client of version 0.4 needs a 0.4 server.

Transport encryption and server hardening. A 0.4 client needs a 0.4 server. With the default Encryption:Mode of Disabled the wire format of 0.3 is unchanged, and a 0.3 client still connects.

Encryption:

  • The whole UDP stream, including LiteNetLib's headers, acknowledgements and disconnect messages, can be encrypted and authenticated. The algorithms are fixed: X25519 with the server's pinned key through the Noise pattern NK (NKpsk0 with a pre-shared key), ChaCha20-Poly1305 records and SHA-256/HKDF. Nothing is negotiated.
  • NetPulse:Encryption: Mode (Disabled, Optional, Required), PrivateKeyFile or NETPULSE_SERVER_PRIVATE_KEY, PreviousPrivateKeyFiles for key rotation, PreSharedKey and PreSharedKeyFile, RequireCookie, CookieLifetimeMs, RekeyAfterPackets, RekeyAfterMs, ReplayWindow, SessionIdleTimeoutMs, ReplaceIdleMs, HandshakeTimeoutMs and PaddingBlock. The server refuses to start in Optional or Required mode without a valid key.
  • NetPulse.Server keygen [--out file] [--force] creates a private key file and prints the public key.
  • A cookie exchange runs before any key agreement and every handshake reply is shorter than its request, so the server cannot be used to amplify traffic. A session can be replaced from the same address only after it has been silent for ReplaceIdleMs, and the old peer is disconnected first, so a new session never inherits an authenticated peer.
  • NetPulse.Common.Security: managed, constant-time X25519 and ChaCha20-Poly1305 without allocations on the packet path, the Noise handshake, cookies, the replay window, record protection with rekeying, and the client and server cores. They are checked against the RFC 7748, 8439 and 5869 vectors and against BouncyCastle, the BCL and an independent Noise implementation, in the test projects only.
  • Plugin SDK: AuthRequest.IsEncrypted and AuthRequest.ChannelBinding (the 32-byte handshake hash), IActor.IsEncrypted.
  • Metrics netpulse.handshakes_ok, handshakes_failed, handshakes_rate_limited, cookies_sent, decrypt_failures, replays, rekeys and plaintext_rejected.
  • NetPulse.TestClient can encrypt: --encrypt --server-public-key KEY [--psk KEY] [--padding N].

Limits (NetPulse:Security, 0 turns a limit off):

  • Per address: MaxConnectionsPerIp, ConnectionAttemptsPerIpPerSecond, HandshakesPerIpPerSecond; server-wide MaxHandshakesPerSecond. They also work without encryption where they apply.
  • Per peer: AuthDeadlineMs, MaxAuthAttempts, token buckets MaxMessagesPerSecond/MessageBurst and MaxBytesPerSecond/ByteBurst, and MaxMessageBytes. A violation disconnects the peer with the reason RateLimited, AuthTimeout or TooManyAuthAttempts.
  • Sizes: MaxUserIdLength, MaxNickNameLength, MaxAuthTokenLength, MaxRoomNameLength, MaxPropertiesPerRoom, MaxPropertyBytes, MaxCachedEventsPerRoom, MaxTargetActors. A request over a limit is refused with InvalidRequest, it is not truncated. Control characters are refused in user ids, nicknames and room names, and removed from text before it is logged.
  • RequireRejoinToken: the server issues a random token on every join and demands it when an inactive player returns, so another client with the same UserId cannot take the seat. New protocol field RejoinToken (ParamKey 56).
  • NetReader refuses more than 4096 nested containers in one message.
  • New metrics netpulse.peers_rate_limited, connections_rejected, auth_timeouts and limit_violations.

Fixes:

  • A client that joined the lobby could receive a stale room list delta right after the full list. The lobby now flushes pending deltas before it adds a subscriber.

Tests: 292 in total, 112 for Common, 34 for the generators and 146 for the server. The new tests include end-to-end runs over real UDP in Disabled, Optional and Required mode through a recording proxy, with replayed, modified, held and dropped datagrams.

Support for the lighter Unity API and the source generator.

Protocol and NetPulse.Common:

  • New value type code Extended (18) with NetTypeRegistry.RegisterExtended, IsExtendedRegistered and UnregisterExtended. An extended value carries a ushort id and a length. A server or client that does not know an id keeps it as an OpaqueValue and forwards it unchanged.
  • NetWriter and NetReader gained sbyte, ulong and char methods.
  • New events Message (244) for typed messages and SyncVarSet (245) for master-owned sync variables.
  • New reserved room property _scene, and RoomPropertyKeys.Scene.
  • RaiseEventRequest.ObjectFlags with the PersistAcrossScenes flag.
  • The join response includes TickRate.

Server:

  • SyncVarSet and changes to _scene are accepted only from the master client.
  • A scene change removes scene objects and objects that are not persistent, together with their cached events.
  • NetPulse:TickRate is now also sent to clients, which use it for their network tick.

Plugin SDK:

  • INetworkObject.IsPersistent.

Tools and tests:

  • NetPulse.Unity.Generators: the Roslyn source generator and analyzers NP0001 to NP0011 for the Unity package, and tools/build-generators.ps1 to copy the built dll into the package.
  • 159 tests: 41 for Common, 34 for the generators and 84 for the server.

The first version in the git history.

  • Async rooms: every room runs on its own fiber that awaits each queued item, so one slow room never delays another room, the lobby or the network thread.
  • Plugin hooks are asynchronous (ValueTask with a CancellationToken) and have a timeout (NetPulse:Plugins:HookTimeoutMs). The synchronous hooks and Defer() were removed. A hook that finishes without a decision counts as Fail.
  • Host API: async timers backed by PeriodicTimer, Enqueue, HttpAsync and RunInBackground.
  • Flood protection per peer (PeerQueueLimit), with a bound on each room queue (RoomQueueCapacity) and the Overloaded disconnect reason.
  • Server-validated network object ownership with three modes (Fixed, Takeover, Request), the operations RequestOwnership and RegisterSceneObjects, and the OwnershipRequested event. The OnBeforeTransferOwnershipAsync hook lets plugins veto transfers.
  • Custom authentication through IAuthPlugin, with AuthTimeoutMs and a server that refuses to start when the configured authentication plugin cannot load. The AuthSample plugin has an HMAC mode and an HTTP mode, and the test client can create tokens with --make-token.
  • Plugin hot reload with isolated load contexts, and the reload console command.
  • Lobby with room list deltas, random join with property filters, player and empty-room time to live, compare-and-set property updates, interest groups and the event cache.
  • Metrics under the meter NetPulse, and the stats, plugins, reload and quit console commands.
  • NetPulse.TestClient, a bot client for smoke tests.
The initial protocol, NetPulse.Common, the lobby and rooms, and the first plugin hooks. This version predates the git history.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: This page explains the vocabulary used by every other page: what the server keeps, who may change what, and which NetPulse feature fits which job. Read it once before the how-to pages.

docs.title: The big picture
docs.text:
A game client connects to one NetPulse server over reliable UDP. The client identifies itself with an AppId and an AppVersion, and the server accepts it or rejects it. Once connected, the client can sit in the lobby, create or join a room, and play. Everything that happens during play is scoped to one room.

The server relays messages and enforces a few rules (ownership, who may change the scene, who may set master variables). It does not run your Unity code. Game logic lives in the clients, and optional server plugins can add validation or authority. See the server overview and getting started.

On the client, everything runs on Unity's main thread. There are no background callbacks, so you can touch Unity objects from any NetPulse event or await continuation.

docs.title: Connection states
docs.text:
Pulse.State moves through these values:

State Meaning Disconnected No connection. The starting and ending state. Connecting The UDP handshake is in progress. Authenticating Connected to the server, waiting for the AppId / token check. Connected Ready to join the lobby or a room. InLobby Receiving the live room list. JoiningRoom A create or join request is in flight. InRoom In a room. Objects, RPCs and messages work only here. Leaving A leave request is in flight.

NetState also declares Disconnecting, but the current client never enters it. Details are on the connecting page.

docs.title: Lobby and rooms
docs.text:
A room is the unit of play. It has a name, a maximum player count (0 means unlimited), an open flag (can others join) and a visible flag (does it appear in the room list), plus custom properties that every member can read. When the last player leaves, the room closes unless the room options ask the server to keep it for a while.

The lobby is an optional directory of visible rooms. Joining the lobby gives you a room list that the server keeps up to date. You do not need the lobby to join a room by name or to join a random room. See matchmaking.

docs.title: Players, ActorId and UserId
docs.text:
Every player in a room has three identifiers:

  • ActorId is a number the server assigns when the player enters the room. It starts at 1 in each new room and counts up. A number is never handed out twice in the same room. Use it to refer to a player inside a room.
  • UserId identifies the person across sessions. The client generates one and stores it in PlayerPrefs, unless Persist User Id is off. An authentication plugin can replace it. A player who disconnects and comes back with the same UserId can reclaim the old slot, with the same ActorId, if the room keeps inactive players.
  • NickName is a display name. It carries no uniqueness guarantee.

The local player is Pulse.LocalPlayer. A player can be inactive: they left with LeaveRoom(true) or lost the connection, and the room keeps their slot for a limited time. See matchmaking.

docs.title: The master client
docs.text:
One player in each room is the master client. The server picks the active player who has been in the room longest, and picks again when that player leaves. Every client is told when it changes.

The master client is an ordinary client with extra duties built into NetPulse:

  • Only the master can load a network scene (scenes).
  • Only the master can change Master sync variables (state sync).
  • Scene objects belong to the master (network objects).
  • RpcTarget.MasterClient delivers to it.

Because it is a client, treat the master as a convenience, not as a trusted authority. The server checks ownership and the master-only rules, and plugins can check more.

docs.title: Events, receivers and caching
docs.text:
Underneath, everything a client sends into a room is an event: an RPC, a typed message, a spawn, a state update. An event has a code, a payload, a set of receivers, a delivery mode, an optional interest group and an optional caching mode.

  • Receivers: everyone else (Others), everyone including the sender (All), the master client only, or a list of specific actors.
  • Delivery: ReliableOrdered, ReliableUnordered, UnreliableSequenced or Unreliable. Reliable modes retransmit, unreliable ones do not.
  • Caching: an event can be stored in the room's cache. The server replays the cache to every player who joins later, which is how late joiners see objects that were spawned before they arrived. Buffered RPCs and spawns use it.

Codes 0 to 199 are free for your own events. Codes 230 to 250 are reserved for the system. Most code never needs to touch event codes: RPCs and messages wrap them. The low-level API page covers Pulse.RaiseEvent.

docs.title: Network objects and ViewId
docs.text:
A network object is a GameObject with a NetworkObject component. Each one has a ViewId, an integer that is the same on every client and names the object in the room.

  • Objects you create with Pulse.Instantiate get a view id of ActorId * 1000 + n. So the actor with id 2 creates objects numbered 2001, 2002 and so on, and each player can have up to 999 live objects at once.
  • Scene objects (placed in the scene in the editor) use their Scene Id, 1 to 999, as the view id.

Every network object has one owner. The owner is the only client that sends the object's state, and the only one whose IsMine is true. Other clients receive the state and apply it. Every NetworkBehaviour on the object (the root and its children) is addressed by its index, so the hierarchy must match on all clients. See network objects.

docs.title: Ownership modes
docs.text:
Each object has an ownership mode, set on the NetworkObject and sent to the server when the object spawns:

Mode Who can become the owner Fixed Nobody. The creator keeps the object. Takeover Anyone, immediately, by requesting it. Request Anyone, but the current owner has to approve.

The server validates every ownership change and every state update, so a client cannot write to an object it does not own. When a player leaves, the objects they own at that moment are destroyed, except scene objects, which return to the master. See ownership.

docs.title: State, RPCs, messages and properties
docs.text:
NetPulse gives you several ways to move data. Pick by the shape of the data:

You want to Use Store room-wide data that late joiners also get (map, round number, score) Room properties, usually typed with RoomKey<T> (rooms and properties) Store per-player data that others can read (team, ready flag) Player properties, with PlayerKey<T> Tell the room something that is not tied to an object (chat, a match event) A typed message (messages) Make something happen on a specific object on other clients (fire, hit, open a door) An RPC (RPC) Keep one value on an object in sync (health, color, score) A SyncVar<T> (state sync) Stream a custom, frequently changing blob for an object [Synced] fields or OnSerialize Move a transform, rigidbody or animator The ready-made components (components)

A rule of thumb: properties are data the room remembers, RPCs and messages are things that happen once, and SyncVar and state sync are values that stay equal across clients.

docs.title: Server time and ticks
docs.text:
The server has a clock. The client estimates the offset to it from the handshake and from a ping every two seconds, and exposes the result as Pulse.ServerTime in seconds. All clients see nearly the same value, which makes it the right basis for interpolation and for timing things that must line up.

The server also announces a tick rate (30 by default). A tick is a numbered slice of server time: Pulse.Tick is floor(ServerTime * TickRate). NetworkBehaviour.OnNetworkTick runs once per tick, and state is sent on tick boundaries. See ticks and time.

docs.title: Interest groups
docs.text:
An interest group limits who receives an event. Group 0 means everyone. An event sent to group 5 reaches only the players who subscribed to group 5 with Pulse.ChangeInterestGroups. You can set a group on a network object so that all its traffic is filtered, and use it for areas, teams or levels of detail. See low-level API.

Two limits apply. Events that go to the master client or to a list of specific actors ignore the group. And the room cache is replayed once, when a player joins, so subscribing to a group later does not deliver the cached events of that group retroactively.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: This page takes you from nothing to a Unity client sitting in a room on your own server. Each step links to the detailed pages.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• The .NET 10 SDK to build and run the server.
  • Unity 2021.3 or newer (6000.x works too) for the client.
  • Git access to the NetPulse repositories. They are private for now.

docs.title: 1. Run the server
docs.text:
Clone the server repository, then build and start it:

git clone https://github.com/Klobiroff/NetPulse-Server.git
cd NetPulse-Server
dotnet build
dotnet run --project src/NetPulse.Server

The build also copies the sample plugin into the server's plugins folder. The server logs the port it listens on:

info: NetPulse.Server.Plugins.PluginManager[0] Loaded plugin NetPulse.Plugins.Sample v1 from NetPulse.Plugins.Sample
info: NetPulse.Server.Networking.NetPulseServer[0] NetPulse server listening on UDP 5055
info: NetPulse.Server.Commands.ConsoleCommandService[0] Console commands: stats, plugins, reload <folder>, quit

The default port is UDP 5055. If a firewall sits between the server and the clients, open that UDP port. See Running the server for the details.

To check the server before you touch Unity, run two test bots against it in a second terminal:

dotnet run --project tools/NetPulse.TestClient -- --bots 2 --room test --seconds 6

The bots join the room test, exchange events and print OK when everything worked.

docs.title: 2. Install the Unity package
docs.text:
The package lives in the Unity repository under Packages/com.netpulse.unity. Open Window > Package Manager, press +, choose Add package from git URL and paste:

https://github.com/Klobiroff/NetPulse-Unity.git?path=Packages/com.netpulse.unity

Unity runs git for you, so the machine needs git installed and credentials that can read the private repository.

No git access?

Copy the folder Packages/com.netpulse.unity from a checkout of the Unity repository into the Packages folder of your project. Unity picks it up on the next domain reload. You can also use Add package from disk and select the package.json inside that folder.

More detail is on the Installation page.

docs.title: 3. Configure the connection
docs.text: Open Project Settings > NetPulse (or NetPulse > Create Settings Asset). Unity creates Assets/Resources/NetPulseSettings.asset. Set the host and port of your server. Leave the AppId empty unless you set NetPulse:AppId on the server. See Settings and editor.

docs.title: 4. Connect and join a room
docs.text:
Add this script to any GameObject in a scene:

using NetPulse;
using NetPulse.Common;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class Demo : MonoBehaviour
{
    private async void Start()
    {
        Pulse.NickName = "Alice";
        await Pulse.Connect();
        var room = await Pulse.JoinOrCreateRoom("arena", new RoomOptions { MaxPlayers = 4 });
        Debug.Log($"Joined {room.Name}, players: {room.PlayerCount}");
    }
}

Press Play. The server log shows Creating room arena for ... for the first player. Run a second copy (a build, or a Multiplayer Play Mode instance) and the player count goes up.

A failed operation throws NetPulseException with the server's ReturnCode. The codes are listed in Codes and keys.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Concepts explains rooms, peers, network objects and ownership.
  • Connecting and Matchmaking cover the lobby and the different ways to join.
  • Network objects and RPC cover gameplay synchronization.
  • Configuration lists every server option, and Writing a plugin shows how to add server logic.

docs.title: Migrating from PUN
docs.text: If you know Photon PUN 2, most of NetPulse will look familiar: rooms, a master client, NetworkObject in the role of PhotonView, [NetRpc] in the role of [PunRPC], ownership modes, custom properties. This page maps the concepts and APIs that NetPulse really has, then lists what differs.

docs.title: Connection and rooms
docs.text: PUN 2 NetPulse PhotonNetwork.ConnectUsingSettings() Pulse.Connect(); settings live in NetPulseSettings PhotonServerSettings (AppId, region) NetPulseSettings (host, port, AppId, AppVersion) PhotonNetwork.GameVersion AppVersion in the settings PhotonNetwork.NickName Pulse.NickName PhotonNetwork.AuthValues Pulse.AuthToken, checked by a server auth plugin PhotonNetwork.NetworkClientState Pulse.State (NetState) PhotonNetwork.IsConnected, InRoom Pulse.IsConnected, Pulse.IsInRoom PhotonNetwork.GetPing() Pulse.RoundTripTimeMs PhotonNetwork.Disconnect() Pulse.Disconnect() PhotonNetwork.OfflineMode Pulse.OfflineMode PhotonNetwork.JoinLobby(), LeaveLobby() Pulse.JoinLobby(), Pulse.LeaveLobby() OnRoomListUpdate(List<RoomInfo>) (changes only) OnRoomListUpdate(IReadOnlyList<RoomInfo>), always the full merged list; also Pulse.LobbyRooms, Pulse.GetRoomList() PhotonNetwork.CreateRoom(name, options) Pulse.CreateRoom(name, options) PhotonNetwork.JoinRoom(name) Pulse.JoinRoom(name) PhotonNetwork.JoinOrCreateRoom(name, options, lobby) Pulse.JoinOrCreateRoom(name, options) PhotonNetwork.JoinRandomRoom(props, maxPlayers) Pulse.JoinRandomRoom(expectedProperties, expectedMaxPlayers, createOptions); can create a room when none matches PhotonNetwork.LeaveRoom(becomeInactive) Pulse.LeaveRoom(becomeInactive) RoomOptions.MaxPlayers, IsVisible, IsOpen Same names in RoomOptions RoomOptions.CustomRoomProperties RoomOptions.CustomProperties RoomOptions.CustomRoomPropertiesForLobby RoomOptions.LobbyProperties RoomOptions.PlayerTtl, EmptyRoomTtl RoomOptions.PlayerTtlMs, EmptyRoomTtlMs PhotonNetwork.CurrentRoom, LocalPlayer, IsMasterClient Pulse.CurrentRoom, Pulse.LocalPlayer, Pulse.IsMasterClient PhotonNetwork.PlayerList Pulse.CurrentRoom.Players PhotonNetwork.MasterClient Pulse.CurrentRoom.MasterClient PhotonNetwork.Time Pulse.ServerTime, in seconds as a double PhotonNetwork.SendRate, SerializationRate Fields of the same name in NetPulseSettings PhotonNetwork.LoadLevel(scene) with AutomaticallySyncScene Pulse.LoadScene(scene) with Auto Sync Scene, master only

docs.title: Players and properties
docs.text: PUN 2 NetPulse Player.ActorNumber Player.ActorId Player.NickName, UserId, IsLocal, IsMasterClient, IsInactive Same names Hashtable custom properties PropertyTable; player.SetProperty(key, value), GetProperty<T>(key) SetCustomProperties(props, expectedProps) SetProperties(delta, expected) (compare-and-set); typed RoomKey<T> and PlayerKey<T> with Set, Get, SetAsync OnRoomPropertiesUpdate(Hashtable) OnRoomPropertiesChanged(PropertyTable), room.OnChanged(key, handler) OnPlayerPropertiesUpdate(Player, Hashtable) OnPlayerPropertiesChanged(Player, PropertyTable), player.OnChanged(key, handler) Room.IsOpen = false room.SetProperty("_isOpen", false), master only

docs.title: Objects, RPCs and state
docs.text:
PUN 2 NetPulse PhotonView NetworkObject MonoBehaviourPun, photonView.IsMine NetworkBehaviour, IsMine photonView.ViewID, PhotonView.Find(id) NetworkObject.ViewId, Pulse.FindObject(viewId) photonView.Owner, OwnerActorNr Owner, OwnerActorId PhotonNetwork.Instantiate("PrefabName", ...) from Resources Pulse.Instantiate(prefab, ...) with the NetworkPrefabRegistry; a name overload exists photonView.InstantiationData (object[]) NetworkObject.InstantiationData (one object) IPunInstantiateMagicCallback.OnPhotonInstantiate OnNetworkSpawned() PhotonNetwork.Destroy(go) Pulse.Destroy(go) [PunRPC] and photonView.RPC("Name", RpcTarget.All, args) [NetRpc] and Rpc.Name(args) or Rpc.To(RpcTarget.All).Name(args); the string form is CallRpc(nameof(Name), RpcTarget.All, args) RpcTarget.All, Others, MasterClient, AllBuffered, OthersBuffered The same names. RpcTarget.Owner is new. There are no ...ViaServer variants. PhotonMessageInfo NetRpcInfo (Sender, SenderActorId, ServerTime) IPunObservable.OnPhotonSerializeView(stream, info) OnSerialize(NetStream stream) stream.IsWriting, SendNext, ReceiveNext() The same, with ReceiveNext<T>(); or stream.Serialize(ref value) for both directions Adding the script to Observed Components Not needed. Any NetworkBehaviour that overrides OnSerialize or has SyncVars is synchronized. PhotonTransformView, PhotonRigidbodyView, PhotonAnimatorView NetworkTransform, NetworkRigidbody, NetworkAnimator OwnershipOption.Fixed, Takeover, Request OwnershipMode.Fixed, Takeover, Request photonView.RequestOwnership(), TransferOwnership(player) networkObject.RequestOwnership(), TransferOwnership(player), plus awaitable ...Async versions OnOwnershipRequest(PhotonView, Player) and approving with TransferOwnership(requester) OnOwnershipRequest(Player) and networkObject.ApproveOwnership(requester) PhotonNetwork.SetInterestGroups, PhotonView.Group Pulse.ChangeInterestGroups, NetworkObject.InterestGroup

PUN has no per-value sync like SyncVar<T>. If you used custom properties or RPCs to mirror one value of an object, SyncVar<T> can replace them (state sync).

docs.title: Events and callbacks
docs.text:
PUN 2 NetPulse MonoBehaviourPunCallbacks NetPulseCallbacks PhotonNetwork.AddCallbackTarget(obj) Pulse.AddCallbackTarget(obj) IConnectionCallbacks INetPulseConnectionCallbacks (OnConnected, OnDisconnected(string cause)) IMatchmakingCallbacks IMatchmakingCallbacks IInRoomCallbacks IRoomCallbacks ILobbyCallbacks ILobbyCallbacks OnConnectedToMaster OnConnected. There is one server and no master/game server hop. PhotonNetwork.RaiseEvent(code, content, options, sendOptions) Pulse.RaiseEvent(code, data, new RaiseEventOptions { ... }), codes 0 to 199 ReceiverGroup, EventCaching, TargetActors ReceiverGroup (plus Targets), CachingOption, TargetActors IOnEventCallback.OnEvent(EventData) IOnEventCallback.OnEvent(code, senderActorId, data) No equivalent C# events on Pulse.Events, for example Pulse.Events.OnJoinedRoom, as an alternative to callback interfaces

The new typed layer has no PUN counterpart: Pulse.Send<T> and Pulse.On<T> for typed room messages (messages).

docs.title: Main differences
docs.text:
• Self-hosted. You run the NetPulse server and connect to its address. There are no regions, no name server and no cloud app id. Server logic is added with plugins (getting started).
  • One entry point, Pulse, not PhotonNetwork. (The name NetPulse is taken by the namespace.)
  • Operations are awaitable. Pulse.Connect(), JoinRoom and the rest return a NetOperation that works with await, yield return and .Completed. The callbacks still exist (async).
  • Source generation. RPCs, SyncVar<T>, messages and [NetSerializable] types are generated at compile time, so classes that use them are partial (analyzers). PUN finds [PunRPC] methods by reflection.
  • No Resources folder for prefabs. Spawning goes through the prefab registry, which is kept up to date by the editor (network objects).
  • Server-enforced ownership. IsMine changes only when the server announces it, including for your own requests, and the server rejects state updates, destroys and master-only operations from the wrong sender (ownership).
  • Master variables. SyncVar<T> with SyncPermission.Master gives the master a value that nobody else may write.
  • Ticks. The server publishes a tick rate, and OnNetworkTick gives a fixed-step callback on every client (ticks and time).
  • NetRpcInfo.ServerTime is the server time on the receiving client when the call ran. PUN's info.SentServerTime is the send time. Put Pulse.ServerTime into the arguments if you need the send time.
  • OnNetworkSpawned waits for the first state of a remote object, so you do not see default values.
  • Scene loading is built in and queues events during the load (scenes).

docs.title: Not available
docs.text: NetPulse has no equivalent for these PUN features: regions and name servers, PhotonNetwork.ReconnectAndRejoin and RejoinRoom (rejoin by calling JoinRoom with the same UserId, see matchmaking), PhotonNetwork.CloseConnection and SetMasterClient from the client (do it with a server plugin), the ...ViaServer RPC targets, friend lists, WebRPC, custom authentication providers (use an auth plugin) and the Photon Chat and Voice products.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Client and connection problems, grouped by symptom. For problems on the server side (logs, limits, plugins, deployment), see operations. The Unity console is the first place to look: NetPulse prefixes its messages with [NetPulse].

docs.title: Connect fails with ConnectionFailed, Timeout or HostUnreachable
docs.text:
The client got no answer from the server. Check, in this order:

  1. The server is running and listens on UDP (not TCP). The default port is 5055.
  2. Host and Port in NetPulseSettings are right. 127.0.0.1 only reaches a server on the same machine.
  3. A firewall or cloud security group allows inbound UDP on that port.
  4. The Connection Key equals the server's ConnectionKey. A mismatch is reported as ConnectionRejected.

docs.title: Connect fails with InvalidAppId, VersionMismatch or AuthenticationFailed
docs.text: Code Cause Fix InvalidAppId (-31) The server has an AppId configured and yours differs Set the same App Id in the settings VersionMismatch (-30) Client and server speak different protocol versions Update the package or the server so both are 0.4 AuthenticationFailed (-32) The auth plugin rejected the token Set Pulse.AuthToken before Connect(), and check the plugin (authentication)

docs.title: Connect fails with SecureHandshakeTimeout or SecureHandshakeFailed
docs.text:
These appear only when Encryption Mode is Required. The server answers a bad handshake with nothing on purpose, so a wrong key looks like a timeout. Check, in this order:

  1. The server runs with NetPulse:Encryption:Mode set to Optional or Required. Against a server in Disabled mode an encrypting client always times out.
  2. Server Public Keys holds the key printed by NetPulse.Server keygen for the private key the server really uses (the server logs its public key at startup). After a server key rotation, ship a build that lists the new key.
  3. The pre-shared key is set on both sides or on neither, with the same value.
  4. The server's Encryption:HandshakeTimeoutMs is not shorter than the time the first packets need to travel.
  5. Nothing in between drops or rewrites UDP packets (a firewall that inspects them, a proxy).

SecureHandshakeFailed means that answers arrived but could not be verified, or that the session reached its counter limit. Reconnecting starts a new session.

docs.title: Connect fails with InvalidConfiguration (-104)
docs.text: Encryption Mode is Required but there is no valid key: Server Public Keys is empty or a key is not a Base64 string of 32 bytes. The Unity console shows which one. Project Settings > NetPulse and the Hub show the same message.

docs.title: The server disconnects the client with RateLimited, AuthTimeout or TooManyAuthAttempts
docs.text: The client broke a limit in NetPulse:Security: too many messages or bytes per second, a message larger than MaxMessageBytes, no authentication within AuthDeadlineMs, or more than MaxAuthAttempts failed authentications. Send less often, split large payloads, or raise the limit on the server. See Security.

docs.title: "Cannot connect while ..." or InvalidState
docs.text: Connect() works only in the Disconnected state, and joins work only from Connected or InLobby. Wait for the earlier operation, or call Pulse.Disconnect() first. Pulse.State shows where the client is.

docs.title: The connection drops when the game freezes or loses focus
docs.text: The transport gives up after 10 seconds without packets. Typical causes are a stalled main thread (a long blocking call or a breakpoint) and Application.runInBackground being off while the window is unfocused. Leave Run In Background on in the settings.

docs.title: A second client in the same project cannot join: "User is already in this room"
docs.text: Both instances read the same UserId from PlayerPrefs, and the server allows one player per UserId in a room. Clones made by Multiplayer Play Mode or by copying the project can share PlayerPrefs. Turn off Persist User Id for the test client, or set a different ConnectionOptions.UserId per instance.

docs.title: Requests time out
docs.text: A request that gets no answer within Request Timeout (10 seconds by default) fails with Timeout (-100). Look for packet loss, a server that is overloaded, or an exception in a server plugin. Raising the timeout hides the cause and only helps on very slow links.

docs.title: Matchmaking
docs.text: Symptom Cause and fix RoomNotFound The name is wrong, or the room already closed. Rooms close when empty unless EmptyRoomTtlMs is set. RoomFull, RoomClosed MaxPlayers reached, or the master set _isOpen to false RoomAlreadyExists CreateRoom with a taken name. Use JoinOrCreateRoom. NoMatchFound from JoinRandomRoom Nothing visible, open and not full matches. Pass createOptions to create a room instead. JoinRandomRoom finds nothing though rooms exist The filter works on lobby properties only. List the key in RoomOptions.LobbyProperties when you create the room. The room list is empty You have to be in the lobby (JoinLobby() from Connected). The list shows visible rooms only, and updates arrive about once a second. After leaving a room, join the lobby again. Rejoin gives a new ActorId The room was created with PlayerTtlMs at 0, the slot expired, or the UserId changed (matchmaking)

docs.title: Objects and spawning
docs.text: Message or symptom Cause and fix Prefab '...' is not in the NetworkPrefabRegistry The prefab has no NetworkObject on its root, is outside the Assets folder, or the registry is stale. Use NetPulse > Rebuild Prefab Registry. Received spawn for unknown prefab id The sending client has a prefab the receiver's registry lacks. Build both from the same project state. Instantiate requires a joined room Wait for JoinRoom to complete before spawning Prefab '...' has no NetworkObject component on its root Add the component to the root, not to a child An object exists only on my machine It was created with Object.Instantiate instead of Pulse.Instantiate, or destroyed with Object.Destroy on another client Only the owner or the master client can destroy Ask the owner or the master to destroy it, for example with an RPC Scene objects have wrong owners Scene ids must be unique and the master registers them after joining. See network objects.

docs.title: The name Rpc does not exist, or a compile error mentions NP00xx
docs.text:
The class is not partial, or the source generator is not active for the assembly. Check:

  • the class and every type that contains it are partial (analyzers);
  • an assembly definition that holds the code references NetPulse.Runtime and NetPulse.Common;
  • Runtime/Analyzers/NetPulse.Generators.dll kept its .meta file (it carries the RoslynAnalyzer label). If you copied the package by hand, copy the .meta files too.

docs.title: An RPC logs "requires a spawned object in a joined room"
docs.text: The call came too early (in Awake or OnEnable) or outside a room. Call RPCs from OnNetworkSpawned or later (lifecycle).

docs.title: "Received an RPC (id ...) that ... does not define"
docs.text: The sender runs a different version of the project, or the receiver's class is not partial and the generator is inactive there. Both sides need the same RPC names.

docs.title: OwnerOnly RPC was not sent
docs.text: The calling client does not own the object. The check is local: ask the owner or change who calls.

docs.title: A SyncVar write is ignored
docs.text: The log says "ignored a write to SyncVar". Only the owner may write an Owner variable and only the master may write a Master variable. Check who owns the object, or change the permission (state sync). The warning appears once per field.

docs.title: A remote value or object never updates
docs.text:
• The owner sends state only for spawned objects, and only on send ticks. Look at Send Rate and Serialization Rate (ticks and time).
  • A list changed in place does not count as a change. Assign a new list to a SyncVar<List<T>>.
  • [Synced] fields raise no event. Poll them, or use SyncVar<T>.
  • The server drops state from a client that does not own the object. The log shows a rejected-message warning.

docs.title: Remote objects move with a long delay
docs.text: Package 0.3.0 computed the automatic interpolation delay of NetworkTransform and NetworkRigidbody as 2 seconds with the default settings. Update to 0.3.1, or set Interpolation Delay on the component to about 0.1 to 0.15 seconds. If the lag remains, check that Interpolation Delay is not set to a large value by hand (components).

docs.title: Ownership
docs.text: Symptom Cause and fix RequestOwnership() does nothing The mode is Fixed (a warning is logged). Use Takeover or Request. A request in Request mode never succeeds The owner has to call ApproveOwnership in OnOwnershipRequest. The server drops the request after its timeout (5 seconds by default). OnOwnershipFailed with Forbidden The mode forbids the change, or a plugin vetoed it. Your local state is unchanged. Objects stay Fixed and never change owner The server is older than the client and predates ownership enforcement (before 0.2). Update the server. IsMine is still false right after RequestOwnership() It changes when the server's event arrives. Use RequestOwnershipAsync or wait for OnOwnerChanged.

docs.title: Scenes
docs.text:
• "The network scene could not be loaded. Is it added to Build Settings?" Add the scene to File > Build Settings.
  • LoadScene warns "Only the master client can load a network scene". Send the master an RPC or a message and let it call LoadScene.
  • Nothing loads on other clients. Auto Sync Scene is off in the settings, or those clients are not in the room.
  • Objects disappear after a load. Only objects with Persist Across Scenes survive, as roots (scenes).
  • RPCs seem to arrive late after a load. Events are held during the load and replayed in order afterwards.

docs.title: Messages and callbacks
docs.text:
• "... is not registered as a message": the type must be partial and implement INetMessage, and it has to exist in the build.
  • "Received a message with unknown id": the sender uses a type the receiver lacks, usually a version mismatch or a renamed type.
  • A handler never fires: check that you subscribed with Pulse.On<T> and kept the returned IDisposable alive, and that the sender used a target that includes you. RpcTarget.Others does not include the sender.
  • Callbacks stop firing in a NetPulseCallbacks subclass: if you override OnEnable or OnDisable, call base.OnEnable() and base.OnDisable(). Pulse.UseTransport resets the client and removes registered targets, so register after it.

docs.title: Builds and platforms
docs.text:
• IL2CPP errors about a missing RPC method: run NetPulse > Tools > Preview IL2CPP link.xml and check that the type is listed (IL2CPP).
  • WebGL: the default transport uses UDP, which browsers do not offer. Supply your own INetTransport (for example over WebSockets) with Pulse.UseTransport (low-level API).
  • The Basic sample does not compile: install the com.unity.inputsystem package, or set the active input handling to the legacy Input Manager (installation).
  • The Traffic tab is empty: statistics are off. Collect Stats is Auto, which means editor and development builds only.
  • With domain reload disabled, Pulse still resets its static state when play mode starts, including the nickname and the auth token. Set them on every run.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: By default the server accepts any client and trusts the UserId and NickName it sends. An authentication plugin changes that: the plugin sees the client's credentials first and decides who gets in and under what identity.

docs.title: IAuthPlugin
docs.text:
public interface IAuthPlugin
{
    Task<AuthResult> AuthenticateAsync(AuthRequest request, CancellationToken ct);
}

AuthRequest carries what the client sent:

Property Description AppId The AppId from the client settings. UserId, NickName What the client claims. Do not trust them. AuthToken The token the client set in its connection options. AuthData An optional PropertyTable with extra values. RemoteEndpoint The client's address as text.

Return AuthResult.Ok(userId, nickName) to accept or AuthResult.Rejected(error) to refuse. The userId and nickName you return replace the client's values for the rest of the session. A null value keeps the client's value, and if both end up empty the server generates a user id and a nickname.

docs.title: What the server does with the answer
docs.text:
• The server checks the AppId and protocol version first. Your plugin runs only for clients that pass them.
  • Rejected, a timeout (NetPulse:Plugins:AuthTimeoutMs, 5 seconds by default) or a cancelled call give the client AuthenticationFailed (-32) with your error message. The server disconnects the client about 250 ms later.
  • An exception inside the plugin also answers AuthenticationFailed with a generic message.
  • A client that is already authenticated gets Ok if it sends the request again.

Authentication is global, not per room. Configure it with NetPulse:Plugins:Auth, the name of the plugin. If that plugin does not load, the server refuses to start. See Security.

docs.title: Packaging
docs.text:
The plugin.json of an authentication plugin names the type in auth. A plugin may have only auth, only factory, or both:

{
  "name": "DevAuth",
  "assembly": "DevAuth.dll",
  "auth": "AuthExamples.DevTokenAuth"
}

The server creates the auth object once per load, and only for the plugin named in NetPulse:Plugins:Auth. It looks for a constructor in this order:

  1. (IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> config, IAuthPluginContext context)
  2. (IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> config)
  3. A parameterless constructor.

config holds the plugin's NetPulse:Plugins:Settings:<Plugin> values. IAuthPluginContext offers a Logger and HttpAsync(request, ct), which sends through the server's HTTP client factory. Throw from the constructor to refuse to start with a bad configuration.

A small plugin for development servers, with tokens listed in the settings:

DevTokenAuth.cs
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using NetPulse.Plugins;

namespace AuthExamples;

public sealed class DevTokenAuth : IAuthPlugin
{
    private readonly Dictionary<string, string> _users = new();
    private readonly IAuthPluginContext _context;

    public DevTokenAuth(IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> config, IAuthPluginContext context)
    {
        _context = context;

        if (!config.TryGetValue("Tokens", out var raw) || string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(raw))
        {
            throw new InvalidOperationException("DevAuth requires a Tokens setting like 'token1=alice,token2=bob'");
        }

        foreach (var pair in raw.Split(',', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries | StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries))
        {
            var parts = pair.Split('=', 2);

            if (parts.Length == 2)
            {
                _users[parts[0]] = parts[1];
            }
        }
    }

    public Task<AuthResult> AuthenticateAsync(AuthRequest request, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        if (request.AuthToken is not null && _users.TryGetValue(request.AuthToken, out var name))
        {
            return Task.FromResult(AuthResult.Ok(name, name));
        }

        _context.Logger.LogWarning("Rejected a login from {Endpoint}", request.RemoteEndpoint);
        return Task.FromResult(AuthResult.Rejected("Unknown token"));
    }
}

Enable it with:

{
  "NetPulse": {
    "Plugins": {
      "Auth": "DevAuth",
      "Settings": {
        "DevAuth": {
          "Tokens": "token1=alice,token2=bob"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: The AuthSample plugin
docs.text:
plugins/NetPulse.Plugins.AuthSample is ready to use. Its plugin name is AuthSample. It is off until you set NetPulse:Plugins:Auth to AuthSample. Build the solution (which copies it next to the server) or publish it into your plugins folder:

dotnet publish plugins/NetPulse.Plugins.AuthSample -c Release -o publish/plugins/AuthSample

Settings go under NetPulse:Plugins:Settings:AuthSample:

Key Default Meaning Mode Hmac Hmac or Http. Anything else stops the server from starting. Secret none Required in Hmac mode. The signing secret. Url none Required in Http mode. An absolute URL.

docs.title: Hmac mode
docs.text:
The plugin verifies tokens offline, with no network call. A token is two base64url parts joined by a dot:

base64url(userId|nickName|expiryUnixSeconds) . base64url(HMACSHA256(secret, payloadBytes))

The server checks the signature in constant time, then the expiry. A bad token gives Invalid token, an old one Token expired. The user id and nickname must not contain |. The secret is never logged.

{
  "NetPulse": {
    "Plugins": {
      "Auth": "AuthSample",
      "Settings": {
        "AuthSample": {
          "Mode": "Hmac",
          "Secret": "change-me-long-random-string"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

Environment variables work too: NetPulse__Plugins__Auth=AuthSample, NetPulse__Plugins__Settings__AuthSample__Mode=Hmac and NetPulse__Plugins__Settings__AuthSample__Secret=....

Your backend creates tokens with the same recipe (see HmacTokens.Create in the plugin source). For testing, the test client prints one:

dotnet run --project tools/NetPulse.TestClient -- --make-token --secret change-me-long-random-string --user user42 --nick Alice --ttl-minutes 60
Flag Default Meaning --make-token Print a token and exit. --secret none Required. The same secret as the server. --user user1 User id inside the token. --nick Player Nickname inside the token. --ttl-minutes 60 Lifetime of the token.

Then connect a bot with it:

dotnet run --project tools/NetPulse.TestClient -- --bots 1 --token <token> --plugin ""

The bot prints bot1 joined 'test' as actor 1, and the server logs Creating room test for user42: the identity came from the token. Without --token the bot fails with authenticate failed (-32 Invalid token). (With --plugin "" the bot's closing self-check reports FAILED because no sample plugin answers its test event. See Running the server.)

docs.title: Http mode
docs.text:
The plugin sends the login to your service. Set Mode to Http and Url to the endpoint:

{
  "Mode": "Http",
  "Url": "https://auth.example/verify"
}

For each login the server sends a POST with a camelCase JSON body made from the request: appId, userId, nickName, authToken, authData and remoteEndpoint. Your service answers with JSON:

{ "ok": true, "userId": "user42", "nickName": "Alice", "message": "", "data": {} }

ok: false rejects the client and message becomes the error. A non-2xx status, an unreachable service or a malformed body also reject the client. The call honours AuthTimeoutMs.

docs.title: Unity client
docs.text:
Pass the token in the connection options:

await Pulse.Connect(new ConnectionOptions
{
    Host = "play.example.com",
    AuthToken = token
});

The server's answer overrides the UserId and NickName the client sent, so the identity other players see in the room comes from your plugin. See Connecting.

docs.title: Hot reload
docs.text: Replacing the files of the auth plugin reloads it, and new logins use the new version. If the reload fails, the previous version keeps working.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: Hooks are the methods of RoomPlugin that the room calls at fixed points. Override the ones you need; the base class continues every call by default.

docs.title: How a hook works
docs.text:
Every hook is a ValueTask method with the same shape:

public override ValueTask OnRaiseEventAsync(IRaiseEventCallInfo info, CancellationToken ct)

info describes the call and carries the decision. ct fires when the hook runs out of time. A hook has to reach a decision before it returns:

Method Meaning info.Continue() Let the action go ahead. info.Fail(message) Reject the action. The client receives PluginReportedError (-20) with your message. info.Cancel() Drop the action quietly. The client receives Ok. Offered only on hooks whose info derives from ICancellableCallInfo.

Every info also has ActorId (the actor that caused the call, or 0 when there is none) and IsProcessed, which is true once a decision has been made.

You can decide before or after an await. The hook can be async, and after each await the code is back on the room fiber, see the room runs one thing at a time.

docs.title: All hooks
docs.text: Hook Runs Fail does Cancel OnCreateRoomAsync When a room is created, before the first player joins. Room is closed, creator gets -20. No OnBeforeJoinAsync A player wants to join and the room is open and not full. Join is refused with -20. No OnJoinAsync The player was added to the room, before the join response. Join is undone, player gets -20. No OnLeaveAsync A player leaves, disconnects or is kicked, before removal. Only logged; the leave goes on. No OnRaiseEventAsync A client raised an event, after the server's own checks, before delivery. Event is not delivered, sender gets -20. Not delivered, sender gets Ok OnBeforeSetPropertiesAsync A client sets room or player properties, after permission checks. Nothing applied, sender gets -20. Nothing applied, sender gets Ok OnSetPropertiesAsync Properties were applied, before the change is broadcast. Only logged. No OnBeforeTransferOwnershipAsync Ownership of a network object is about to change or be requested. Change refused with -20. Nothing changes, sender gets Ok OnBeforeCloseRoomAsync The room is empty, or the server is shutting down. Room stays open, unless the close is forced. Same as Fail OnCloseRoomAsync The room is closing. No effect. No OnUnhandledExceptionAsync Plugin code threw. Not a decision hook.

docs.title: OnCreateRoomAsync
docs.text:
Runs once, after the factory created the plugin and before the creator joins. The info has Options (the RoomOptions the client sent), UserId, NickName and PlayerProperties. Use it to reject room settings that your game does not allow.

RoomLimitsPlugin.cs
using NetPulse.Plugins;

namespace HookExamples;

public sealed class RoomLimitsPlugin : RoomPlugin
{
    private const int MaxPlayersLimit = 16;

    public RoomLimitsPlugin(IPluginHost host)
        : base(host)
    {
    }

    public override ValueTask OnCreateRoomAsync(ICreateRoomCallInfo info, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        if (info.Options.MaxPlayers is 0 or > MaxPlayersLimit)
        {
            info.Fail($"MaxPlayers must be between 1 and {MaxPlayersLimit}");
            return default;
        }

        info.Continue();
        return default;
    }
}

docs.title: OnBeforeJoinAsync and OnJoinAsync
docs.text:
The join sequence is: the server checks that the room is open and not full, then runs OnBeforeJoinAsync, adds the player, runs OnJoinAsync, sends the join response, announces PlayerJoined to the others and replays the event cache to the newcomer.

OnBeforeJoinAsync has UserId, NickName, IsRejoin and PlayerProperties. For a new player, the PlayerProperties table you leave behind becomes the player's initial properties, so you can add or remove keys. ActorId is the existing actor id on a rejoin and 0 otherwise. This is the place for checks that need I/O, such as a ban list:

BanCheckPlugin.cs
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using NetPulse.Plugins;

namespace HookExamples;

public sealed class BanCheckPlugin : RoomPlugin
{
    private readonly string _banServiceUrl;

    public BanCheckPlugin(IPluginHost host, string banServiceUrl)
        : base(host) => _banServiceUrl = banServiceUrl;

    public override async ValueTask OnBeforeJoinAsync(IBeforeJoinCallInfo info, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var url = $"{_banServiceUrl}?user={Uri.EscapeDataString(info.UserId)}";
        using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, url);

        try
        {
            using var response = await Host.HttpAsync(request, ct);

            if (response.IsSuccessStatusCode)
            {
                info.Fail("You are banned from this room");
                return;
            }
        }
        catch (HttpRequestException ex)
        {
            Host.Logger.LogWarning(ex, "Ban service is unreachable, letting {User} in", info.UserId);
        }

        info.Continue();
    }
}

OnJoinAsync has the new Actor (an IActor) and IsRejoin. The player is already in Host.Actors, but its client has not received the join response yet. Anything you send to that client from inside the hook arrives before the response. Use Host.Enqueue to send after the join has finished, as in Writing a plugin. If you fail OnJoinAsync, the server rolls the join back.

docs.title: OnLeaveAsync
docs.text:
Runs for every way a player can leave: a LeaveRoom request (reason left), a disconnect (reason disconnect), or a kick (the reason you passed to Host.KickActor). info.Actor is still in the room. IsInactive is true when the player stays as an inactive actor so that it can rejoin, which happens when the room has PlayerTtlMs set and the player disconnected or asked to become inactive.

The hook runs once per leave. When an inactive player's time to live expires later, the player is removed without another OnLeaveAsync. A failed OnLeaveAsync cannot keep the player in the room.

When the whole room closes, players are removed without OnLeaveAsync. Use OnCloseRoomAsync for work that happens at the end of the room.

docs.title: OnRaiseEventAsync
docs.text:
Runs for every event a client raises: your own events (codes 0 to 199) and the object events: instantiate, destroy, RPC, state sync, message and master sync variable. The server has already refused reserved codes and ownership violations by then, see Security. The info.Request is a RaiseEventRequest with EventCode, Data, Receivers, TargetActors, InterestGroup, Caching, Delivery and ViewId.

The request is mutable. If you continue, the event goes out as it is when the hook returns, so you can rewrite Data, change Receivers or Caching. If Data arrives as an OpaqueValue (a custom type that the server does not know), you can read it with NetReader.

ChatRulesPlugin.cs
using NetPulse.Plugins;

namespace HookExamples;

public sealed class ChatRulesPlugin : RoomPlugin
{
    private const byte ChatEvent = 20;
    private const int MaxLength = 200;

    private readonly HashSet<int> _muted = new();

    public ChatRulesPlugin(IPluginHost host)
        : base(host)
    {
    }

    public void Mute(int actorId) => _muted.Add(actorId);

    public override ValueTask OnRaiseEventAsync(IRaiseEventCallInfo info, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        if (info.Request.EventCode != ChatEvent)
        {
            info.Continue();
            return default;
        }

        if (_muted.Contains(info.ActorId))
        {
            info.Cancel();
            return default;
        }

        if (info.Request.Data is not string text || text.Length > MaxLength)
        {
            info.Fail("Chat messages must be text of up to 200 characters");
            return default;
        }

        info.Continue();
        return default;
    }
}

This hook sits on the path of every RPC and state sync of every player, so keep the common case fast: check the event code first and call Continue() right away for everything you do not care about.

docs.title: OnBeforeSetPropertiesAsync and OnSetPropertiesAsync
docs.text:
OnBeforeSetPropertiesAsync runs after the server's permission checks (reserved keys, other players' properties) and before the properties are applied. TargetActorId is 0 for room properties and the actor id for player properties. Properties is the change (a null value deletes a key) and ExpectedProperties is the compare-and-set condition the client attached, or null. The server evaluates the condition after the hook, so a hook that continues does not skip the check.

Fail to reject with a message, or cancel to ignore the change without telling the client anything is wrong. The Security page has an example.

OnSetPropertiesAsync runs after the properties were applied and before they are broadcast. It has TargetActorId and Properties. It cannot undo anything: use it to react, for example to recompute a derived value.

docs.title: OnBeforeTransferOwnershipAsync
docs.text:
Runs when ownership of a network object is about to change, and when a player asks for an object in Request mode. The info has ViewId, NewOwnerActorId, CurrentOwnerActorId, OwnershipMode and IsRequest. IsRequest is true for the first step of a Request-mode object, when the server is about to forward the request to the owner. The later transfer, when the owner approves, runs the hook again with IsRequest set to false.

LockedObjectsPlugin.cs
using NetPulse.Plugins;

namespace HookExamples;

public sealed class LockedObjectsPlugin : RoomPlugin
{
    private readonly HashSet<int> _locked = new();

    public LockedObjectsPlugin(IPluginHost host)
        : base(host)
    {
    }

    public void Lock(int viewId) => _locked.Add(viewId);

    public void Unlock(int viewId) => _locked.Remove(viewId);

    public override ValueTask OnBeforeTransferOwnershipAsync(IBeforeTransferOwnershipCallInfo info, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        if (_locked.Contains(info.ViewId))
        {
            info.Fail($"Object {info.ViewId} is locked");
            return default;
        }

        info.Continue();
        return default;
    }
}

docs.title: OnBeforeCloseRoomAsync and OnCloseRoomAsync
docs.text:
OnBeforeCloseRoomAsync runs when the last player left (reason empty, after EmptyRoomTtlMs if the client set one) and when the server shuts down (reason server shutdown). Fail or cancel keeps the emptied room alive. The server will ask again the next time the room becomes empty. The shutdown ignores the answer and closes the room anyway. Host.CloseRoom() also skips this hook.

OnCloseRoomAsync always runs when a room closes. The Reason is one of empty, server shutdown, closed by plugin, or a creation failure (plugin initialization failed, create rejected by plugin, create failed).

When OnCloseRoomAsync starts, the room has already stopped its timers and cancelled the token of RunInBackground, the players are gone, and broadcasting reaches nobody. What is left is the time to save results. Await the work inside the hook; HookTimeoutMs applies.

MatchResultPlugin.cs
using System.Net.Http.Json;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using NetPulse.Plugins;

namespace HookExamples;

public sealed class MatchResultPlugin : RoomPlugin
{
    private readonly string _resultsUrl;

    public MatchResultPlugin(IPluginHost host, string resultsUrl)
        : base(host) => _resultsUrl = resultsUrl;

    public override async ValueTask OnCloseRoomAsync(ICloseRoomCallInfo info, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, _resultsUrl)
        {
            Content = JsonContent.Create(new { room = Host.RoomName, reason = info.Reason, closedAtMs = Host.ServerTimeMs })
        };

        try
        {
            using var response = await Host.HttpAsync(request, ct);
            response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();
        }
        catch (HttpRequestException ex)
        {
            Host.Logger.LogWarning(ex, "Could not save the result of room {Room}", Host.RoomName);
        }

        info.Continue();
    }
}

docs.title: OnUnhandledExceptionAsync
docs.text:
public virtual ValueTask OnUnhandledExceptionAsync(Exception ex, ICallInfo? info)

The room calls it when plugin code throws: a hook, a timer callback, or an action passed to Host.Enqueue. info is the call that failed, or null when the exception did not come from a hook. The default implementation logs the exception. Override it to report errors elsewhere. The room keeps running, and the failed call gets Fail.

If this method throws itself, the room logs that and carries on.

docs.title: Errors and timeouts
docs.text:
• A hook that throws, or whose ValueTask faults, goes to OnUnhandledExceptionAsync, increments the plugin error counter shown by the stats command, and fails the call with the message Plugin error.
  • A hook that returns without a decision is logged as an error and fails with Plugin did not respond.
  • Every hook has NetPulse:Plugins:HookTimeoutMs (5 seconds by default) to finish, and so does the plugin factory. When time runs out, the call fails with Plugin hook timed out, the server logs a warning and cancels ct. The room then moves on. A Continue() that arrives later is ignored with a warning. Pass ct to every await that supports it, otherwise the abandoned hook keeps running in the background.
  • Calling Continue, Fail or Cancel a second time is ignored with a warning. The first decision wins.
  • Exceptions that happen after an await are caught the same way as those before it.

Timeouts are logged but do not call OnUnhandledExceptionAsync.

docs.title: Host API
docs.text: IPluginHost is what a plugin uses to read and change its room. Each room has its own host, and RoomPlugin exposes it as Host. The factory receives the same host in CreateAsync.

docs.title: Reading the room
docs.text:
Member Type Description RoomName string Name of the room. Actors IReadOnlyList<IActor> A snapshot of every actor in the room, including inactive ones, in join order. MasterClientId int Actor id of the master client, or 0 when nobody is active. The master is the longest-present active player. RoomProperties PropertyTable The live room properties. Read it freely; change it through SetRoomProperties so that clients are told. ServerTimeMs long Milliseconds since the server started. It is the same clock that clients receive as server time. Logger ILogger Logger in the category NetPulse.Room.<room name>. GetActor(actorId) IActor? One actor, or null. GetNetworkObject(viewId) INetworkObject? One registered network object, or null. NetworkObjects IReadOnlyCollection<INetworkObject> A snapshot of all registered network objects.

IActor has ActorId, UserId, NickName, Properties, IsInactive and IsMasterClient. An inactive actor is a player who disconnected and may rejoin; it receives no events.

INetworkObject has ViewId, CreatorActorId, OwnerActorId, OwnershipMode, IsSceneObject and IsPersistent. For a scene object nobody has taken, OwnerActorId reports the current master.

Read room state only on the room fiber

Actors, GetActor, RoomProperties, NetworkObjects and GetNetworkObject read the room directly. Use them inside hooks, timer callbacks, Enqueue actions and after an await in a hook. Do not touch them from RunInBackground or from a thread you started. Logger, ServerTimeMs, RoomName and HttpAsync are safe anywhere.

docs.title: Acting on the room
docs.text:
Member Description BroadcastEvent(code, data, receivers, targets, caching, delivery, senderActorId) Send an event to players. SetRoomProperties(props, broadcast) Merge properties into the room. SetPlayerProperties(actorId, props, broadcast) Merge properties into one player. KickActor(actorId, reason) Remove a player from the room. CloseRoom() Close the room. CreateTimer(...), Enqueue(...), HttpAsync(...), RunInBackground(...) See Timers, HTTP and background work.

These methods are safe to call from any thread. Called from the room fiber, they take effect immediately. Called from elsewhere, they are queued and run on the fiber.

docs.title: BroadcastEvent
docs.text:
void BroadcastEvent(
    byte code,
    object? data,
    ReceiverGroup receivers = ReceiverGroup.All,
    int[]? targets = null,
    CachingOption caching = CachingOption.DoNotCache,
    DeliveryMode delivery = DeliveryMode.ReliableOrdered,
    int senderActorId = 0);
  • code is the event code. Use 0 to 199 for your own events, the same range clients may raise.
  • data is any value the wire format supports: numbers, strings, arrays, PropertyTable, or types registered with NetTypeRegistry. See Wire protocol.
  • receivers is Others, All, MasterClient or Targets. Targets sends to the actor ids listed in targets. Inactive actors never receive events.
  • caching controls the event cache that late joiners receive. An event cached with senderActorId 0 belongs to the server and stays until removed, even after players leave.
  • senderActorId is what clients see as the sender. 0 means the server. With sender 0, Others reaches everyone.

Events from a plugin skip OnRaiseEventAsync. Clients receive them like any other event.

docs.title: SetRoomProperties and SetPlayerProperties
docs.text:
Both merge the table into the existing properties; a null value deletes a key. With broadcast true (the default) all players receive a properties-changed event; the sender id in that event is 0 (the server).

These calls do not run OnBeforeSetPropertiesAsync and are not subject to the reserved-key rule, so a plugin can set _isOpen, _isVisible, _maxPlayers and _scene itself. The lobby list is updated after a room change. SetPlayerProperties ignores an unknown actor id.

docs.title: KickActor and CloseRoom
docs.text:
KickActor tells the player with an ErrorInfo event (Forbidden and your reason), then removes it from the room. OnLeaveAsync runs with the reason you gave and IsInactive false. The player stays connected to the server and can join another room.

CloseRoom sends every player an ErrorInfo event with RoomClosed, then closes the room. OnBeforeCloseRoomAsync is skipped and OnCloseRoomAsync runs with the reason closed by plugin.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A plugin that lets the master client run two commands with event 70: kick <actorId> and close. It also stamps each joining player with the join time as a player property.

AdminCommandsPlugin.cs
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using NetPulse.Common;
using NetPulse.Plugins;

namespace HostExamples;

public sealed class AdminCommandsPlugin : RoomPlugin
{
    public const byte CommandEvent = 70;
    public const byte NoticeEvent = 71;

    public AdminCommandsPlugin(IPluginHost host)
        : base(host)
    {
    }

    public override ValueTask OnJoinAsync(IJoinCallInfo info, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        Host.SetPlayerProperties(info.Actor.ActorId, new PropertyTable { ["joinedAtMs"] = Host.ServerTimeMs });
        info.Continue();
        return default;
    }

    public override ValueTask OnRaiseEventAsync(IRaiseEventCallInfo info, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        if (info.Request.EventCode != CommandEvent)
        {
            info.Continue();
            return default;
        }

        if (info.ActorId != Host.MasterClientId)
        {
            info.Fail("Only the master client can run commands");
            return default;
        }

        Run(info.Request.Data as string ?? string.Empty);
        info.Cancel();
        return default;
    }

    private void Run(string command)
    {
        var parts = command.Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);

        if (parts.Length == 2 && parts[0] == "kick" && int.TryParse(parts[1], out var actorId) && Host.GetActor(actorId) is { } target)
        {
            Host.BroadcastEvent(NoticeEvent, $"{target.NickName} was kicked");
            Host.KickActor(actorId, "Kicked by the master client");
            return;
        }

        if (parts.Length == 1 && parts[0] == "close")
        {
            Host.Logger.LogInformation("Room {Room} closed by command", Host.RoomName);
            Host.CloseRoom();
            return;
        }

        Host.Logger.LogWarning("Unknown command '{Command}'", command);
    }
}

The command event is cancelled, so it never reaches the other players, and the sender gets Ok when it asked for a response.

docs.title: Hot reload
docs.text: With NetPulse:Plugins:HotReload enabled (the default), you can replace a plugin while the server runs. Players stay connected and running rooms are not interrupted.

docs.title: What happens when files change
docs.text:
1. The server watches the plugin directory, including subfolders. Any change inside a plugin folder starts a half-second timer for that folder. Further changes restart the timer, so copying several files produces one reload.
  2. The server loads plugin.json and the assembly from that folder into a new isolated load context. The files are read into memory, so nothing stays locked and you can overwrite them again at any time.
  3. If the load works, the new version takes the plugin's name. Rooms created from now on use it.
  4. Rooms that already run the plugin keep the old version until they close. When the last of them has closed, the old version is unloaded.

The log shows Loaded plugin <name> v<N> from <folder>. The number is the server-wide load counter, so it rises with every load of any plugin.

If the load fails, for example because the dll is half copied or the manifest is invalid, the server logs Failed to load plugin from <folder>; keeping previous version if any and the previous version stays active. The next file change triggers another attempt.

Other cases:

  • A new folder with a valid manifest loads as a new plugin.
  • Deleting a plugin folder unloads the plugin. Running rooms finish on it, and rooms that ask for it afterwards get PluginNotFound.
  • If the plugin is the one named in NetPulse:Plugins:Auth, a successful reload replaces the authentication plugin for new logins.

docs.title: Reloading by hand
docs.text:
The console command forces a reload of one folder, even with HotReload off:

reload GreeterPlugin

It takes the folder name, prints reloaded or reload failed and writes the details to the log. Use plugins to check which plugins are loaded and how many rooms use each.

With HotReload set to false the server loads plugins only at startup, plus whatever you reload by hand.

docs.title: What to keep in mind
docs.text:
• State lives in the room's plugin object. A room never switches versions, so its fields stay consistent. A new room starts with fresh state.
  • Each version has its own copy of static fields. Do not use statics to share data between rooms that may run different versions.
  • Settings come from appsettings.json and environment variables when the server starts. Changing them needs a restart. A plugin reload gives the factory the same settings as before.
  • Anything that outlives the room and references plugin code can keep the old version in memory: a thread you started, a timer you did not dispose, a static event subscription. Stop your own threads in DisposeAsync or OnCloseRoomAsync.
  • A change in the contract between plugin and clients, for example a new meaning of an event code, affects rooms differently depending on the version they run. Roll such changes out with a restart if mixed versions would confuse clients.
  • The shared assemblies (NetPulse.Plugins, NetPulse.Common) come from the server and cannot be hot reloaded. Updating the SDK needs a server restart and a rebuilt plugin.

docs.title: Disposal
docs.text:
When a room closes, the server calls DisposeAsync on its plugin object. Override it if the plugin holds resources.

public override ValueTask DisposeAsync()
{
    _client.Dispose();
    return default;
}

On server shutdown the same happens for every room, and all load contexts are unloaded afterwards.

docs.title: Plugins overview
docs.text: A plugin is a .NET class library that the server loads from a folder and runs inside your rooms. Use one when the server must make a decision that clients cannot be trusted with: validating events, keeping authoritative scores, checking an allow-list before a join, or driving a match with a timer.

docs.title: What a plugin can do
docs.text:
• Intercept room activity through hooks: create, join, leave, raise event, property changes, ownership transfers and room close. A hook can let the action through, change it, drop it or reject it. See Hooks.
  • Act on the room through the host API: broadcast events, set room and player properties, kick players, close the room. See Host API.
  • Run timers, call HTTP services and do background work. See Timers, HTTP and background work.
  • Authenticate clients before they reach any room. See Authentication.

docs.title: The pieces
docs.text:
Piece Role plugin.json Manifest in the plugin folder: name, assembly, factory type, optional auth type. IPluginFactory Created once per loaded plugin version. The server calls CreateAsync every time a room that uses the plugin is created. RoomPlugin The object that receives hooks. Each room gets its own instance, so its fields are per-room state. Derive from this base class and override only the hooks you need. IPluginHost What the plugin uses to act on its room. The base class exposes it as Host.

Rooms pick a plugin by name through RoomOptions.Plugin. Rooms that do not name one use NetPulse:Plugins:Default, and if that is empty they run without a plugin.

docs.title: The room runs one thing at a time
docs.text:
Every room has its own queue and a single consumer, called a fiber. The fiber takes one item from the queue (a client message, a join, a leave, a timer start), runs it to completion, including every await inside it, and only then takes the next one. The lobby has its own fiber, and so does every other room.

This model has four consequences:

  • Code of one room never runs in parallel with other code of that room. You need no locks around room state, fields of your plugin or Host.RoomProperties.
  • After an await inside a hook you are back on the room fiber, so touching room state is still safe. Do not use ConfigureAwait(false) or Task.Run in code that touches room state.
  • A slow hook stalls only its own room. While a hook waits on a database, the room handles nothing else, because the order of messages matters more than latency. Other rooms, the lobby and the network thread keep working. A hook that never finishes is cut off after HookTimeoutMs.
  • Timer callbacks and other continuations are not queue items. They run on the same fiber, but they can run while a hook is suspended at an await. Two pieces of code never run at the same instant, yet they can interleave at await points.

Work whose result does not change the outcome of a call, such as analytics or saving a match result, belongs in Host.RunInBackground so that the room does not wait for it.

docs.title: Plugin versions and hot reload
docs.text: The server loads a plugin into its own collectible load context. When you overwrite the files, new rooms use the new version and running rooms finish on the old one. See Hot reload.

docs.title: The sample plugins
docs.text:
The repository contains two plugins under plugins/:

  • NetPulse.Plugins.Sample keeps an authoritative score per player, broadcasts a timer tick every second and rejects one event code. It shows hooks, a factory with settings, and a timer.
  • NetPulse.Plugins.AuthSample is an IAuthPlugin with an HMAC token mode and an HTTP mode. See Authentication.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text: Start with Writing a plugin, which builds a plugin from an empty project to a loaded one.

docs.title: Testing plugins
docs.text:
There are three levels, from quick to thorough: run the server with bot clients, unit-test hooks against fakes, and run the real server in-process inside a test. This page uses one small plugin for all three.

ScoreCapPlugin.cs
using NetPulse.Plugins;

namespace ScoreCap;

public sealed class ScoreCapPlugin : RoomPlugin
{
    public const byte ScoreEvent = 30;
    public const int MaxPoints = 100;

    public ScoreCapPlugin(IPluginHost host)
        : base(host)
    {
    }

    public override ValueTask OnRaiseEventAsync(IRaiseEventCallInfo info, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        if (info.Request.EventCode == ScoreEvent && info.Request.Data is int points && points > MaxPoints)
        {
            info.Fail($"At most {MaxPoints} points per event");
            return default;
        }

        info.Continue();
        return default;
    }
}

public sealed class ScoreCapFactory : IPluginFactory
{
    public ValueTask<PluginCreateResult> CreateAsync(IPluginHost host, string pluginName, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> config, CancellationToken ct) =>
        ValueTask.FromResult(PluginCreateResult.Ok(new ScoreCapPlugin(host)));
}

docs.title: Level 1: a real server and bots
docs.text:
Install the plugin as described in Writing a plugin, start the server and run the test client:

dotnet run --project tools/NetPulse.TestClient -- --bots 2 --room test --plugin ScoreCap --seconds 3

The joined lines show that the bots connected, authenticated and passed your join hooks. A failed hook shows up as join failed (-20 <your message>). The client's final verdict is written for the sample plugin and reports FAILED for any other plugin, so read the lines instead of the exit code. The server log shows load errors, timeouts and exceptions. This level suits a first look. It cannot assert on what a plugin sent.

docs.title: Level 2: unit tests with fakes
docs.text:
Hooks are plain methods that receive an interface, so you can call them directly. Write a fake for IPluginHost and one for each call info you use. The fake records the decision and the events the plugin broadcast.

Fakes.cs
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions;
using NetPulse.Common;
using NetPulse.Plugins;

namespace ScoreCap.Tests;

public enum FakeOutcome
{
    Pending,
    Continued,
    Failed,
    Cancelled
}

public sealed class FakeRaiseEventCall : IRaiseEventCallInfo
{
