The registry is rebuilt for you when a prefab under Assets is imported, moved or deleted, and before every build. Ids are assigned once per prefab (by its asset GUID) and never reused, so the table stays stable between builds. Prefabs outside the Assets folder, for example inside packages, are not picked up. To rebuild by hand, use NetPulse > Rebuild Prefab Registry or the button in Project Settings and in the Hub.

Because the ids come from the registry, client and server builds that talk to each other should be built from the same project state. The error "Received spawn for unknown prefab id" means the other side has a prefab yours lacks.

docs.title: Instantiate and destroy
docs.text:
using NetPulse;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class Spawner : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private GameObject _playerPrefab;

    private GameObject _player;

    private async void Start()
    {
        await Pulse.Connect();
        await Pulse.JoinOrCreateRoom("arena");
        _player = Pulse.Instantiate(_playerPrefab, new Vector3(0f, 1f, 0f), Quaternion.identity, Color.red);
    }

    private void OnDestroy()
    {
        if (_player != null)
        {
            Pulse.Destroy(_player);
        }
    }
}

Pulse.Instantiate(prefab, position, rotation, data, interestGroup) creates the object on your client immediately, makes you its owner and tells everyone else to create it. The server caches the spawn, so players who join later receive it too. It returns the new GameObject, or null after logging an error if you are not in a room (offline mode counts as a room), the prefab is not in the registry, or the prefab has no NetworkObject on its root.

The optional data argument travels with the spawn. Every client reads it from NetworkObject.InstantiationData as soon as the object exists, which is the way to pass a color, a team or a seed. It can be anything the dynamic serializer handles: numbers, string, Guid, arrays, a PropertyTable, and the Unity types Vector2, Vector3, Quaternion, Color, Vector2Int and Vector3Int.

using NetPulse;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class Tinted : NetworkBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private Renderer _renderer;

    public override void OnNetworkSpawned()
    {
        if (NetworkObject.InstantiationData is Color color)
        {
            _renderer.material.color = color;
        }
    }
}

The interestGroup argument applies to the spawn event itself: only players subscribed to that group create the object. The object's later traffic (state, RPCs) uses the Interest Group set in its NetworkObject inspector, so give both the same value.

There is also an overload Pulse.Instantiate(string prefabName, ...) that looks the prefab up by its name in the registry. Names must be unique for it to be reliable.

Pulse.Destroy(gameObject), Pulse.Destroy(networkObject) and networkObject.Destroy() remove the object on every client and drop its cached events from the room. Only the owner or the master client may do it; anyone else gets a warning and nothing happens.

  • A plain Object.Destroy(gameObject) on a networked object removes it on your client only. The others keep their copy.
  • Scene objects cannot be destroyed over the network. Pulse.Destroy on one only destroys your local copy.
  • When a player leaves the room, the objects they own at that moment are destroyed on every client. Objects they had already handed to someone else stay. A player who is only inactive keeps their objects.
  • When you leave the room or lose the connection, all non-scene network objects are destroyed locally.

docs.title: What a NetworkObject tells you
docs.text:
Member Meaning ViewId The room-wide id (concepts) IsSpawned Registered and live in the room IsMine, Owner, OwnerActorId Who owns it. IsMine is also true when you are not in a room. OwnershipMode The mode set in the inspector InstantiationData, PrefabId What the spawn carried IsSceneObject, SceneId Scene object info InterestGroup, PersistAcrossScenes Inspector settings Behaviours The NetworkBehaviours on it

Inside a NetworkBehaviour you also get NetworkObject, IsMine, Owner, ViewId and IsSpawned directly. Pulse.FindObject(viewId) returns the object with that id, or null.

docs.title: Scene objects
docs.text:
Objects that sit in the scene at design time can be networked too: a door, a pickup, a shared cube. Tick Scene Object on the NetworkObject. The inspector assigns the next free Scene Id (1 to 999) and uses it as the object's view id. Scene ids have to be unique within a scene; a duplicate is reassigned when you save, with a warning.

Scene objects behave a little differently:

  • They are not spawned over the network. Each client has its own copy from the loaded scene, and the copies find each other by view id.
  • They belong to the master client. The master tells the server about them, with their ownership modes, after it joins and again after it becomes master. A scene object that someone took over and who then left returns to the master.
  • They cannot be destroyed over the network and cannot persist across scenes.
  • When the master loads a new network scene, the scene objects of the old scene are gone and the new scene's objects register after the load (scenes).

docs.title: Persist across scenes
docs.text: A root network object with Persist Across Scenes ticked survives Pulse.LoadScene. NetPulse calls DontDestroyOnLoad on it and tells the server to keep it. All other non-scene network objects are destroyed locally when a network scene starts loading, and the server forgets them. See scenes.

docs.title: Offline mode
docs.text:
Offline mode runs the same NetPulse API against a local, in-memory room. There is no server and no socket. It lets a single-player mode, a tutorial or a test use exactly the code that the online game uses.

Switch it on before connecting, while the state is Disconnected:

using NetPulse;
using NetPulse.Common;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class StartGame : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private bool _singlePlayer;
    [SerializeField] private GameObject _playerPrefab;

    private async void Start()
    {
        Pulse.OfflineMode = _singlePlayer;
        await Pulse.Connect();
        await Pulse.JoinOrCreateRoom("main", new RoomOptions { MaxPlayers = 4 });
        Pulse.Instantiate(_playerPrefab, Vector3.zero, Quaternion.identity);
    }
}

Changing OfflineMode in any other state logs an error and does nothing. To switch, call Pulse.Disconnect() first.

docs.title: What the API does offline
docs.text:
Area Behavior Connect() Succeeds at once and raises OnConnected. The user id comes from the settings as usual. Lobby JoinLobby() moves to InLobby. GetRoomList() returns an empty list. Rooms CreateRoom, JoinRoom, JoinOrCreateRoom and JoinRandomRoom all create a local room (named OfflineRoom if you pass no name). The local player is actor 1 and the master. The RoomOptions limits and CustomProperties are applied. OnCreatedRoom and OnJoinedRoom fire. Properties Applied locally and immediately. A compare-and-set does not compare: the new value is written. RPCs, messages, RaiseEvent Delivered to your own handlers when the target includes you: All, AllBuffered, MasterClient, Owner or your own Player. Others and OthersBuffered reach nobody. Objects Pulse.Instantiate creates the object locally, and the prefab registry is not needed. Owner state is never sent, so OnSerialize is not called. SyncVar<T> still raises Changed for local writes. Ownership RequestOwnership() makes you the owner at once. Fixed objects still refuse. Time and ticks ServerTime is the local clock. The tick rate is 30, and OnNetworkTick runs as usual. Scenes Pulse.LoadScene works, because you are the master. Stats RoundTripTimeMs is 0 and no traffic is counted.

The code path is the same as online, so bugs in game logic show up offline too. What offline cannot show you is anything that depends on a second player or on the network: ordering between clients, ownership contention, interpolation of remote objects.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Keep the online and offline paths down to one if at start-up, as above. Everything after Connect() can stay the same.
  • A game that offers both modes can let the player choose, then call Disconnect() and flip OfflineMode when they return to the menu.
  • Because ownership always succeeds offline, test the Request and Fixed rules against a real server as well.

docs.title: Ownership
docs.text: Every network object has one owner, and only the owner sends the object's state. The server keeps the registry of owners and checks every change, so a client never decides by itself that it owns something. IsMine and Owner change only when the server's ownership event arrives, including for requests you sent yourself.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
The mode is the Ownership Mode field of the NetworkObject (OwnershipMode in code). It is sent to the server with the spawn.

Mode Who can become the owner Fixed Nobody. The creator keeps the object. RequestOwnership and TransferOwnership are refused. Takeover Anyone. RequestOwnership() takes it at once. The owner or the master can also hand it to a player with TransferOwnership(player). Request RequestOwnership() asks the current owner, who can approve. Only the owner or the master can assign with TransferOwnership(player).

The master can reassign any object that is not Fixed.

docs.title: Requesting and approving
docs.text:
In Request mode the owner receives the request as OnOwnershipRequest(Player requester). The owner answers by calling ApproveOwnership(requester). Denying means doing nothing: the request expires on the server (after 5 seconds by default, a server setting) and the requester is not told. A requester can have one pending request per object at a time.

using NetPulse;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class Crate : NetworkBehaviour
{
    public override void OnOwnershipRequest(Player requester)
    {
        if (requester.GetProperty("team", 0) == Owner.GetProperty("team", 0))
        {
            NetworkObject.ApproveOwnership(requester);
        }
    }

    public override void OnOwnerChanged(Player previous, Player current) => Debug.Log($"Now owned by {current?.NickName}");

    public void Grab() => NetworkObject.RequestOwnership();
}

OnOwnershipRequest runs only on the owner's client. The same request is also raised as Pulse.Events.OnOwnershipRequest(networkObject, requester) and through IOwnershipCallbacks (connecting). ApproveOwnership works only for the current owner; others get a warning.

docs.title: Waiting for the result
docs.text:
RequestOwnership() and TransferOwnership() return immediately and do not tell you the outcome. The async versions do:

using NetPulse;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class Pickup : MonoBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField] private NetworkObject _target;

    public async void TryGrab()
    {
        var granted = await _target.RequestOwnershipAsync(3f);
        Debug.Log(granted ? "Got it" : "Refused or timed out");
    }

    public async void Give(Player player)
    {
        var moved = await _target.TransferOwnershipAsync(player);
        Debug.Log(moved ? "Handed over" : "Not handed over");
    }
}
Call Result true when Result false when RequestOwnershipAsync(timeoutSeconds = 5) You are the owner (already, or after the server confirms) The mode is Fixed, you are not in a room, the server refuses, or the time runs out TransferOwnershipAsync(player, timeoutSeconds = 5) The player is the owner (already, or after confirmation) Same reasons as above

The operations return a NetOperation<bool> and never throw for a refusal. See async.

docs.title: What happens when ownership changes
docs.text: When the server announces a change, each NetworkBehaviour on the object gets OnOwnerChanged(previous, current) and then OnOwnershipGained() or OnOwnershipLost(). After all behaviours, NetworkObject.OwnershipChanged and Pulse.Events.OnOwnershipChanged are raised. The new owner starts sending the object's full state. Components adapt: NetworkRigidbody, for example, makes the body kinematic on non-owners (components). The exact order is on the lifecycle page.

docs.title: Failures
docs.text:
When the server rejects an ownership operation (Forbidden, ObjectNotFound), the client logs a warning and raises Pulse.Events.OnOwnershipFailed(networkObject, returnCode, message). The local state stays as it was, and a pending async call completes with false. The server also rejects state updates, spawns and destroys from the wrong sender, and the client logs at most one warning per second about those.

A server plugin can veto or change transfers. See hooks. A vetoed request looks like a request that was never approved.

docs.title: Scene objects and leaving players
docs.text:
• Scene objects belong to the master (OwnerActorId 0 means "the master"). The master registers their modes with the server after it joins and after it becomes master, so a Takeover scene object can be grabbed by anyone.
  • When a player leaves, the scene objects they had taken return to the master.
  • Other objects owned by the player at that moment are destroyed on every client. Objects they had handed to someone else survive. A player who is only inactive keeps their objects.
  • Destroying a network object requires being the owner or the master.

In offline mode, RequestOwnership() makes you the owner immediately (offline mode).

The Basic sample has a shared Takeover cube: press E to take it, then move it with the arrow keys.

docs.title: Rooms and properties
docs.text: Once you are in a room, Pulse.CurrentRoom is a Room and every member, including you, is a Player. Both can carry properties: small values that the server stores, that every member can read, and that late joiners receive when they join.

docs.title: Room and Player
docs.text:
Room members:

Member Meaning Name, MaxPlayers, IsOpen, IsVisible The room's settings (see matchmaking) MasterClientId, MasterClient The current master LocalPlayer You Players, PlayerCount All players, ordered by ActorId; inactive players are included GetPlayer(actorId), TryGetPlayer(actorId, out player) Look up by actor id GetNextPlayer(after) The player with the next higher ActorId, wrapping around to the first Properties The raw PropertyTable

Player members: ActorId, NickName, UserId, IsLocal, IsInactive, IsMasterClient and Properties.

using NetPulse;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class RoomPrinter : MonoBehaviour
{
    private void Print()
    {
        var room = Pulse.CurrentRoom;
        if (room == null)
        {
            return;
        }

        foreach (var player in room.Players)
        {
            var tags = (player.IsMasterClient ? " master" : string.Empty) + (player.IsLocal ? " you" : string.Empty);
            Debug.Log($"#{player.ActorId} {player.NickName}{tags}");
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Typed keys
docs.text:
A RoomKey<T> or PlayerKey<T> ties a property name to a value type, so the compiler checks both. Declare each key once as a static readonly field and use it everywhere.

using System;
using NetPulse;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class Scores : MonoBehaviour
{
    private static readonly RoomKey<int> Score = new("score");
    private static readonly PlayerKey<string> Mood = new("mood");

    private IDisposable _scoreWatch;
    private IDisposable _moodWatch;

    private void OnEnable() => Pulse.Events.OnJoinedRoom += Subscribe;

    private void OnDisable()
    {
        Pulse.Events.OnJoinedRoom -= Subscribe;
        _scoreWatch?.Dispose();
        _moodWatch?.Dispose();
    }

    public void AddPoint()
    {
        var room = Pulse.CurrentRoom;
        room.Set(Score, room.Get(Score) + 1);
    }

    private void Subscribe()
    {
        var room = Pulse.CurrentRoom;
        _scoreWatch = room.OnChanged(Score, value => Debug.Log($"Score is {value}"));
        _moodWatch = Pulse.LocalPlayer.OnChanged(Mood, (player, value) => Debug.Log($"{player.NickName} feels {value}"));
        Pulse.LocalPlayer.Set(Mood, "happy");
    }
}

The API on Room and Player is the same shape:

Call Meaning Get(key, defaultValue) Reads the local copy. Returns defaultValue (or default) if the key is missing or not convertible. Set(key, value) Writes. The local copy and the OnChanged handlers update at once, and the change goes to the server and the other clients. SetAsync(key, value, expected) Compare-and-set. Returns a NetOperation. See below. OnChanged(key, handler) Subscribes to changes of one key. Returns an IDisposable that unsubscribes.

For a PlayerKey<T>, the handler receives the Player and the new value. OnChanged fires for your own writes too, and for the other clients' changes when they arrive. It fires for a key only when that key is part of the change.

Numbers convert between numeric types, so a key declared as RoomKey<int> reads a value another client stored as a long. A key that is missing reads as the default.

docs.title: Who may write
docs.text:
Any member can write room properties and its own player properties. Writing another player's properties is allowed only to the master client. The reserved room keys _isOpen, _isVisible, _maxPlayers and _scene are master-only as well. Set applies the change locally before the server has answered. If the server refuses it, NetPulse logs a warning and restores the previous value of every key that nobody has changed since, and OnChanged fires again with the restored value. Set does not tell you about the rejection in code. When you need to know whether a write was accepted, use the compare-and-set form, which waits for the server.

Writing null removes a key. A typed Set cannot pass null for a value type, so remove with the raw API: room.SetProperty("score", null).

docs.title: Compare-and-set
docs.text:
SetAsync(key, value, expected) succeeds only if the stored value still equals expected. The server checks and applies it atomically, and the local copy changes only after the server accepts. A mismatch fails the operation with PropertyCasFailed (-15). This is how several clients can claim a slot or increment a counter without overwriting each other.

using NetPulse;
using NetPulse.Common;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class ClaimHost : MonoBehaviour
{
    private static readonly RoomKey<string> Host = new("host");
    private static readonly RoomKey<int> Round = new("round");

    private async void Claim()
    {
        var room = Pulse.CurrentRoom;

        try
        {
            await room.SetAsync(Host, Pulse.LocalPlayer.NickName, expected: null);
            Debug.Log("You are the host");
        }
        catch (NetPulseException e) when (e.ReturnCode == ReturnCode.PropertyCasFailed)
        {
            Debug.Log($"{room.Get(Host)} got there first");
        }
    }

    private async void NextRound()
    {
        var room = Pulse.CurrentRoom;
        var current = room.Get(Round);
        await room.SetAsync(Round, current + 1, current);
    }
}

A missing key never equals a number. If round was never set, SetAsync(Round, 1, 0) fails, because the server compares "absent" with 0. Create the room with the key in CustomProperties so it exists, or use null as expected through the raw API described next.

docs.title: The raw PropertyTable
docs.text:
Typed keys sit on top of string keys and PropertyTable (in NetPulse.Common). The raw API is useful when keys are built at runtime or when you set several properties in one request.

using NetPulse;
using NetPulse.Common;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class RawProperties : MonoBehaviour
{
    private async void Start()
    {
        var room = Pulse.CurrentRoom;

        room.SetProperty("map", "forest");
        var map = room.GetProperty<string>("map", "unknown");

        var delta = new PropertyTable { ["round"] = 2, ["phase"] = "fight" };
        var expected = new PropertyTable { ["round"] = 1 };
        await Pulse.Client.SetRoomProperties(delta, expected);

        Pulse.LocalPlayer.SetProperty("team", 1);
        var team = Pulse.LocalPlayer.GetProperty<int>("team");
        Debug.Log($"{map} team {team} {room.Properties.Count} properties");
    }
}
Call Meaning room.SetProperty(key, value), player.SetProperty(key, value) Set one key. null removes it. room.SetProperties(delta, expected), player.SetProperties(delta) Set several keys in one request. expected makes it a compare-and-set; every key in expected must match, and a key with a null value matches a missing key. GetProperty<T>(key, defaultValue) Read one key. Pulse.Client.SetRoomProperties(delta, expected), Pulse.Client.SetPlayerProperties(player, delta, expected) Same as above but return a NetOperation you can await. Properties The PropertyTable itself: Get<T>, TryGet<T>, ContainsKey, Remove, Keys, Count, Merge, Matches, Clone.

Property values may be bool, byte, short, int, long, float, double, string, Guid, arrays of byte, int, float, string or object, a nested PropertyTable, the Unity types Vector2, Vector3, Quaternion, Color, Vector2Int and Vector3Int, and types marked [NetSerializable]. The messages page lists what a [NetSerializable] type can contain. Any other type throws a serialization exception when sent.

docs.title: Change notifications
docs.text: Besides OnChanged, you can listen to every change with Pulse.Events.OnRoomPropertiesChanged and OnPlayerPropertiesChanged (or the IRoomCallbacks interface, see connecting). They deliver only the changed keys as a PropertyTable, not the whole table. Your own writes raise these events immediately; a compare-and-set raises them once the server has accepted it.

docs.title: RPC
docs.text: A remote procedure call runs a method of a network object on other clients. Mark the method with [NetRpc], then call it through the generated Rpc property. The compiler checks the arguments, and nothing is looked up by name at runtime.

docs.title: Declaring and calling
docs.text:
using NetPulse;
using NetPulse.Common;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed partial class Hero : NetworkBehaviour
{
    [NetRpc(RpcTarget.Others)]
    private void Hit(int damage, Vector3 at, NetRpcInfo info) => Debug.Log($"{info.Sender?.NickName} hit for {damage} at {at}");

    [NetRpc(RpcTarget.MasterClient, Delivery = DeliveryMode.Unreliable, OwnerOnly = true)]
    private void Report(string text) => Debug.Log(text);

    public void Attack(Player victim)
    {
        Rpc.Hit(10, transform.position);
        Rpc.To(RpcTarget.All).Hit(10, transform.position);
        Rpc.To(victim).Report("attacked");
    }
}
  • Rpc.Hit(10, position) sends to the target named in the attribute.
  • Rpc.To(RpcTarget.All).Hit(...) overrides the target for one call.
  • Rpc.To(player).Report(...) sends to one player.

The attribute is [NetRpc(RpcTarget target = RpcTarget.All, Delivery = ..., OwnerOnly = ...)]. Without arguments the target is All and the delivery is ReliableOrdered.

Requirements:

  • The class derives from NetworkBehaviour and is partial. sealed partial works and keeps the generated Rpc property private. In a non-sealed class the property is protected, so subclasses can use it and outside code cannot. Add a public method like Attack above for callers.
  • The method returns void, has no ref, out or in parameters, is not static, generic or abstract, and has a name that no other method in the class uses. RPC overloads are not allowed, because the RPC id is a hash of the method name.
  • A NetRpcInfo parameter is optional and must come last. It is filled in by the receiver and is not part of the call.
  • The method can have any access level.

The analyzer reports violations as compile errors; see analyzers (NP0001 to NP0005).

docs.title: Parameter types
docs.text: An RPC takes the same types as a message: bool, byte, sbyte, short, ushort, int, uint, long, ulong, float, double, char, string, Guid, enums, the Unity vectors, Quaternion, colors and Rect, Player, NetworkObject, [NetSerializable] and INetMessage types, and arrays or List<T> of those. For anything else, pass its fields as separate parameters or mark a type [NetSerializable].

docs.title: Targets
docs.text:
RpcTarget Runs on All Every client, including the caller. The caller's copy runs immediately, inside the call. Others Every client except the caller MasterClient The master. If the caller is the master, it runs locally. Owner The object's owner. If the caller is the owner, it runs locally. For a scene object without an explicit owner, the owner is the master. AllBuffered Like All, and the server also stores the call and replays it to clients that join later OthersBuffered Like Others, with the same storage

Rpc.To(player) sends to one player. If that player is you, it runs locally.

Buffered RPCs are tied to the object. The server drops the stored calls of an object when the object is destroyed, so a late joiner does not replay RPCs of an object that no longer exists. Use buffering for state that new players must catch up on, such as "door opened", and prefer a SyncVar or a property when the value is simply the latest one, because a buffered call is replayed every time it was made.

docs.title: Delivery
docs.text: Delivery selects the transport mode: ReliableOrdered (default), ReliableUnordered, UnreliableSequenced or Unreliable. An unreliable RPC may be lost, so use it only for repeated, disposable calls such as a cosmetic effect.

docs.title: NetRpcInfo and OwnerOnly
docs.text:
A trailing NetRpcInfo parameter gives the receiver three values:

Member Meaning Sender The Player who called. null if that player has left. SenderActorId The sender's actor id ServerTime The server time on this client at the moment the call ran

OwnerOnly = true makes the calling client refuse the call unless it owns the object: it logs a warning and sends nothing. The check happens on the caller only. Receivers do not verify that the sender owns the object, so a modified client could still send the call. For anything that matters, validate on the receiving side with info.Sender or info.SenderActorId, or on the server with a plugin.

using NetPulse;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed partial class Door : NetworkBehaviour
{
    [NetRpc(RpcTarget.MasterClient)]
    private void RequestOpen(NetRpcInfo info)
    {
        if (info.Sender == null)
        {
            return;
        }

        Rpc.To(RpcTarget.AllBuffered).SetOpen(true);
    }

    [NetRpc(RpcTarget.All)]
    private void SetOpen(bool open) => transform.localRotation = Quaternion.Euler(0f, open ? 90f : 0f, 0f);

    public void Use() => Rpc.RequestOpen();
}

docs.title: When can you call?
docs.text:
The object must be spawned and the client must be in a room. Otherwise the call logs an error and does nothing. Call RPCs from OnNetworkSpawned or later, not from Awake or OnEnable (lifecycle).

Received RPCs run on the main thread. If the object does not exist on a receiver yet, the call is dropped there. Events that arrive while a network scene is loading are held and replayed in order afterwards (scenes).

docs.title: Old style calls
docs.text: The previous API, CallRpc("Name", target, args), still works on [NetRpc] methods but uses reflection and string names. It is covered under low-level API, and the analyzer (NP0011) suggests the generated call instead.

docs.title: Scenes
docs.text:
Network scenes keep every player of a room in the same Unity scene. The master client calls Pulse.LoadScene, and every client, including players who join later, loads the same scene. Events that arrive during the load are held back and replayed in order afterwards.

using NetPulse;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class ArenaFlow : NetPulseCallbacks
{
    [SerializeField] private GameObject _propPrefab;

    public async void StartArena()
    {
        if (!Pulse.IsMasterClient)
        {
            return;
        }

        try
        {
            await Pulse.LoadScene("Arena");
        }
        catch (NetPulseException e)
        {
            Debug.LogError($"Could not load: {e.Message}");
        }
    }

    public override void OnNetworkSceneLoaded(string sceneName)
    {
        Debug.Log($"Scene ready: {sceneName}");

        if (Pulse.IsMasterClient)
        {
            Pulse.Instantiate(_propPrefab, Vector3.zero, Quaternion.identity);
        }
    }
}

Add every scene you load to File > Build Settings. If the scene cannot be loaded, an error is logged and the load operation fails with InvalidState.

docs.title: Loading
docs.text:
Pulse.LoadScene(string sceneName) and Pulse.LoadScene(int buildIndex) work like this:

  • Only the master client may call them. Anyone else gets a warning and an operation that fails with Forbidden. Outside a room they fail with InvalidState. To let other players trigger a load, send the master a message or an RPC and let it call LoadScene.
  • The master writes the room property _scene with the value "{loadId}:{nameOrIndex}". The loadId grows with every load, so clients can tell a new request from one they already handled. Clients cannot write this property themselves.
  • Every client, the master included, loads the scene asynchronously with a single-mode SceneManager.LoadSceneAsync.
  • The returned operation completes on the master after the scene has loaded. On the other clients, OnNetworkSceneLoaded is the signal.

If a second LoadScene starts before the first one finishes, the newer load wins and the older operation fails with NetPulseReturnCode.Cancelled. The same happens when the client leaves the room or disconnects during a load. Awaiting such an operation throws NetPulseException.

docs.title: Auto sync
docs.text: Auto Sync Scene in the settings (on by default, settings and editor) turns the loading on. With it off, Pulse.LoadScene only sets the _scene property and completes immediately, and nobody loads the scene automatically. That mode suits games that manage scenes themselves and just want a shared "current scene" value.

docs.title: Late joiners
docs.text:
When a player enters a room, the client reads _scene. If the room is already in another scene, the client loads it. If the active scene already matches, nothing happens and OnNetworkSceneLoaded is not raised for that player, so do not rely on the callback for setup that every player needs. Objects that were spawned in the scene arrive from the server's cache as usual.

The match is by scene name or by build index, whichever form the master used.

docs.title: What happens to objects
docs.text:
When a load begins, on every client:

  • Network objects that are not scene objects and do not have Persist Across Scenes are destroyed locally. The server forgets them and drops their cached events.
  • Objects with Persist Across Scenes (root objects, marked DontDestroyOnLoad) survive and keep their owner.
  • Scene objects of the old scene disappear with the scene. After the load, the new scene's objects register, and the master re-registers them with the server.

docs.title: Event queueing
docs.text:
From the moment a load starts until it ends, room events are held in a queue: RPCs, state updates, typed messages, RaiseEvent events, spawns and destroys. When the scene is ready, the scene objects are registered, the queue is replayed in the original order, and then OnNetworkSceneLoaded(sceneName) is raised. The effect is that no RPC or spawn hits an object that does not exist yet.

Property changes, player joins and leaves, and ownership and master events are not queued. The queue holds up to 4096 events. Beyond that the newest events are dropped and a warning is logged. If you leave the room or disconnect during a load, the queue is discarded.

docs.title: Callbacks
docs.text:
Pulse.Events.OnNetworkSceneLoaded passes the loaded scene's name. A NetPulseCallbacks subclass can override OnNetworkSceneLoaded, and a class that implements ISceneCallbacks can register with Pulse.AddCallbackTarget.

The Basic sample shows the flow with two scenes and a pair of master-only buttons that load them. Its player prefab has Persist Across Scenes on, so the players stay when the scene changes.

docs.title: Settings and editor
docs.text: This page lists every field of NetPulseSettings, then the editor windows and menu items that NetPulse adds.

docs.title: NetPulseSettings
docs.text:
The settings are a ScriptableObject asset. The client loads it at runtime with Resources.Load("NetPulseSettings"), so it has to sit in a Resources folder. The default location is Assets/Resources/NetPulseSettings.asset. If no asset exists, the client uses a temporary instance with the defaults below. To use a different asset in code, pass it to Pulse.Connect(settings) (connecting).

Create the asset with NetPulse > Create Settings Asset, with the button in Project Settings > NetPulse, or with Assets > Create > NetPulse > Settings.

docs.title: Server
docs.text: Field Default Meaning Host 127.0.0.1 Server address (IP or host name) Port 5055 Server UDP port App Id empty Identifies your game. If the server is configured with an AppId, the two must match. App Version 1.0 Your build's version string. It is sent to the server, which does not check it. Connection Key NetPulse Shared secret of the UDP handshake. It has to equal the server's ConnectionKey.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Field Default Meaning Encryption Mode Off Off sends plain packets. Required encrypts everything and refuses plain packets, see Connecting. Server Public Keys empty One or more Base64 public keys printed by NetPulse.Server keygen. The inspector and the Hub check the format. Several keys are only for rotating the server key. Pre Shared Key empty Optional Base64 key (32 bytes) that the server also has. It ships in the build and can be extracted. Rekey After Packets 1000000 Replace the sending key after this many packets (0 = never by count) Rekey After Ms 600000 Replace the sending key after this long (0 = never by time) Replay Window 4096 Packets remembered for replay protection. A multiple of 64, 64 to 65536. Padding Block 0 0 is off, otherwise 16 to 512. Pads every packet to a multiple of this size. Use the same value as the server. Handshake Timeout 5 (at least 0.5) Seconds to wait for the secure handshake before the connection fails with SecureHandshakeTimeout

docs.title: Player
docs.text: Field Default Meaning Default Nick Name empty Used when Pulse.NickName was not set. If it is empty too, the client picks Player plus a random number. Persist User Id on Keep the generated UserId in PlayerPrefs. Needed for rejoining.

docs.title: Rates
docs.text:
Field Default Meaning Send Rate 20 (1 to 60) Upper limit for state sends per second Serialization Rate 0 (0 to 60) Second limit for state sends. 0 means the server tick rate. The effective rate is the lower of the two. Request Timeout 10 (at least 1) Seconds before a request fails with Timeout

How the two rates turn into a send interval is shown in ticks and time.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
Field Default Meaning Run In Background on Pulse.Connect turns on Application.runInBackground so the connection stays alive without focus Auto Sync Scene on Let Pulse.LoadScene load the scene on every client (scenes) Collect Stats Auto Auto collects traffic statistics in the editor and development builds only. Always and Never override that. Log Verbose off Reserved. The current client does not read it. Prefab Registry none The NetworkPrefabRegistry asset used for spawning. Created and filled automatically.

In code the same values are properties of NetPulseSettings, for example settings.SendRate = 30. CollectStats is a bool property there: reading it applies the Auto rule, and setting it chooses Always or Never.

docs.title: Project Settings
docs.text: Edit > Project Settings > NetPulse draws all fields of the asset. It has two buttons: Rebuild Prefab Registry and Open Hub. Without an asset it shows a notice and a Create Settings Asset button.

docs.title: The NetPulse Hub
docs.text:
NetPulse > Open Hub opens a window with two tabs. It updates four times a second while the game runs.

The Overview tab shows:

  • Connection: state, online or offline mode, ping, server time, user id and nickname. In Play Mode there are Connect and Disconnect buttons.
  • Security: the encryption mode, the number of pinned server keys, any problem with the key format, and in Play Mode whether the session is encrypted.
  • Room: name, player count against the limit, the open and visible flags, the number of network objects and the player list, with markers for yourself, the master and inactive players.
  • Traffic: messages and kilobytes sent and received, with the current kilobytes per second.
  • Prefab registry: how many prefabs are registered, and a Rebuild Prefab Registry button.

docs.title: Traffic tab
docs.text:
The Traffic tab is a profiler for the traffic of the running client. It needs Play Mode and Collect Stats on (the Collect toggle at the top switches it live). Reset clears the counters. The top line shows the current bytes per second, and the second line the session totals.

The table has one row per entry, with columns Category, Name, In B/s, Out B/s, In total, Out total and Msgs in/out. Click a column header to sort by it, and click again to reverse the order. The popup and the text box above the table filter by category and by name.

Categories:

Category One row per NetworkObject Network object (viewId name): its spawn, destroy, state and RPC traffic Rpc RPC method (Type.Method) Message Message type StateSync Object state updates (a single row) SyncVar Behaviour type that sends Master variables System Protocol traffic: Request op N, Response op N, Event N, Ping, Pong

The categories overlap on purpose. An RPC counts under Rpc and also under the NetworkObject it belongs to, so do not add the rows together. The rate columns use a window of one second.

You can read the same data in code:

using NetPulse;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class TrafficLog : MonoBehaviour
{
    private void Dump()
    {
        var stats = Pulse.Stats;
        Debug.Log($"in {stats.BytesInPerSecond:F0} B/s, out {stats.BytesOutPerSecond:F0} B/s, session {stats.TotalBytesIn + stats.TotalBytesOut} B");

        foreach (var entry in stats.Entries)
        {
            if (entry.Category == StatCategory.Rpc)
            {
                Debug.Log($"{entry.Name}: {entry.MessagesOut} sent, {entry.BytesOut} B");
            }
        }
    }
}

NetStats exposes Enabled, Entries (each NetStatEntry has Category, Name, BytesIn, BytesOut, MessagesIn, MessagesOut, BytesInPerSecond and BytesOutPerSecond), the Total... counters, BytesInPerSecond, BytesOutPerSecond and Reset(). When collection is off, the counters cost nothing.

docs.title: NetworkObject inspector
docs.text: The inspector for NetworkObject shows Ownership Mode, Interest Group, Persist Across Scenes and the Scene Object toggle with its Scene Id (an error appears outside 1 to 999). The scene object toggle is disabled on prefab assets and when several objects are selected. On a prefab asset a notice reminds you that it is added to the registry automatically. In Play Mode a read-only Runtime block shows View Id, Owner Actor, Is Mine and Spawned.

docs.title: Menu items
docs.text:
Menu What it does NetPulse > Create Settings Asset Creates or selects the settings asset NetPulse > Open Settings Opens Project Settings > NetPulse NetPulse > Open Hub Opens the Hub window NetPulse > Rebuild Prefab Registry Scans Assets for prefabs with a NetworkObject and updates the registry NetPulse > Tools > Preview IL2CPP link.xml Writes and shows the generated link.xml (IL2CPP) NetPulse > Samples > Build Basic Sample Scene Builds the Basic sample scenes (import the sample first, installation) Assets > Create > NetPulse > Settings and Network Prefab Registry Create the two assets by hand Add Component > NetPulse Network Transform, Network Rigidbody, Network Animator

The registry also rebuilds itself when prefabs under Assets are imported, moved or deleted, and before each build.

docs.title: State sync
docs.text: State sync keeps values on a network object equal on every client. NetPulse offers SyncVar<T> for most cases, and [Synced] fields plus OnSerialize for streaming custom data. Built-in components such as NetworkTransform use the same machinery (components).

docs.title: Which one to use
docs.text:
Need Use A value with a change callback: health, score, a color, a name SyncVar<T> A value that only the master may change SyncVar<T> with SyncPermission.Master A value that was set once and is read by newcomers A room or player property if it is not tied to an object, otherwise SyncVar<T> A one-time event on an object An RPC Custom data that changes constantly, written by hand (aim direction, a compressed path) OnSerialize with NetStream A few primitives with no callbacks, in older code [Synced] fields

New code should reach for SyncVar<T> first. It is type-safe, supports many more types than [Synced], and tells you when the value changed.

docs.title: SyncVar
docs.text:
using NetPulse;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed partial class Hero : NetworkBehaviour
{
    private readonly SyncVar<int> _health = new(100);
    private readonly SyncVar<string> _title = new(string.Empty, SyncPermission.Master);

    public int Health => _health.Value;

    public override void OnNetworkSpawned() => _health.Changed += (previous, current) => Debug.Log($"{name}: {previous} -> {current}");

    public void Damage(int amount) => _health.Value -= amount;

    public void Rename(string title) => _title.Value = title;
}

Rules:

  • Declare the field readonly inside a partial class that derives from NetworkBehaviour. The source generator registers it. The analyzer warns about a field that is not readonly or is outside a NetworkBehaviour (NP0008), and rejects an unsupported T (NP0007).
  • T can be any type listed under serializable types: primitives, strings, enums, Unity vectors and colors, Player, NetworkObject, arrays, lists and [NetSerializable] types.
  • Read with .Value, or rely on the implicit conversion to T.
  • Changed(previous, current) fires on every client when the value changes, for your own writes and for values that arrive from the network. An exception in a handler is logged and does not stop the other handlers.
  • Assigning a value equal to the current one does nothing. Equality is EqualityComparer<T>.Default, so for arrays and lists it compares references. Changing the contents of a list in place is not noticed; assign a new list to publish the change.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Permission Who may write How it travels Owner (default) The owner of the object As a delta inside the object's regular state update, on a tick boundary Master The master client As its own message, sent in the next frame after the write

A write by someone without permission is ignored, and one warning per field is logged. The write is accepted while the object is not yet spawned or you are not in a room, so initial values can be set freely. The server rejects state updates from non-owners and master variables from non-masters as well.

A behaviour can have up to 32 Owner variables. Extra ones are not synchronized, and an error is logged. The total limit across both kinds is 256 per behaviour.

docs.title: Late joiners
docs.text: A player who joins later receives the full value of every variable: owners resend their full state when someone enters, and the master sends its variables to the newcomer. For a remote object whose behaviours have state, OnNetworkSpawned waits until that first state has been applied, for at most one second, so the first thing the callback sees is real data (lifecycle).

docs.title: Streaming custom data with OnSerialize
docs.text:
Override OnSerialize(NetStream stream) to write and read your own bytes. The owner's call has stream.IsWriting true, and every other client's call has stream.IsReading true. The Serialize(ref value) form is symmetric, so one body handles both directions.

using NetPulse;
using NetPulse.Common;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class AimSync : NetworkBehaviour
{
    private Vector3 _aim;
    private int _ammo;
    private float _heat;

    public Vector3 Aim => _aim;

    public int Ammo => _ammo;

    public float Heat => _heat;

    protected override DeliveryMode SerializeDelivery => DeliveryMode.UnreliableSequenced;

    public override void OnSerialize(NetStream stream)
    {
        stream.Serialize(ref _aim);
        stream.Serialize(ref _ammo);
        stream.Serialize(ref _heat);
    }
}

NetStream offers:

  • Serialize(ref x) for bool, byte, short, int, long, float, double, string, byte[], Vector2, Vector3, Quaternion and Color, and Serialize(INetSerializable) for your own types that implement Serialize(NetStream).
  • SendNext(object) and ReceiveNext<T>() for the PUN style. The type you read must match the type you wrote exactly, or you get default.
  • IsWriting, IsReading, Remaining (bytes left to read) and Timestamp, the server time at which the owner produced the state.
using NetPulse;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class PunStyleSync : NetworkBehaviour
{
    private int _ammo;
    private Vector3 _lookAt;

    public override void OnSerialize(NetStream stream)
    {
        if (stream.IsWriting)
        {
            stream.SendNext(_ammo);
            stream.SendNext(_lookAt);
            return;
        }

        _ammo = stream.ReceiveNext<int>();
        _lookAt = stream.ReceiveNext<Vector3>();
    }
}

How it is sent: on each send tick the owner calls OnSerialize, compares the bytes with the previous ones and sends only when they differ. Because it runs on every send tick for every owned object, keep it cheap and avoid allocations.

Override SerializeDelivery to pick the delivery mode of a behaviour's state. The default is ReliableOrdered. For UnreliableSequenced and Unreliable, state is also resent once after one second of silence, so a lost packet cannot leave a client stale for long. Behaviours with different delivery modes on one object go out in separate packets.

docs.title: Synced fields
docs.text:
[Synced] marks a field of a NetworkBehaviour for automatic sync, without a callback:

using NetPulse;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class Scoreboard : NetworkBehaviour
{
    [Synced] private int _score;
    [Synced] private Color _tint = Color.white;

    public int Score => _score;

    public Color Tint => _tint;

    public void Add(int points) => _score += points;
}

Supported types are bool, byte, short, int, long, float, double, string, Vector2, Vector3, Quaternion, Color, Vector2Int, Vector3Int and enums; the analyzer rejects others (NP0010). Fields are sorted by name, at most 32 per behaviour, and the owner polls them on each send tick through reflection and sends the ones that changed. A receiving client writes the field directly, so you get no event and have to poll or check it in Update. Prefer SyncVar<T> when you need to react to a change.

docs.title: Send rate
docs.text: State goes out on tick boundaries, only from the owner, and only for objects that are spawned. The rate is the lower of Send Rate and Serialization Rate in the settings, where Serialization Rate = 0 means the server tick rate. Ticks and time shows the arithmetic. A change you make in OnNetworkTick is included in the update sent at the end of that same tick.

docs.title: Ticks and time
docs.text: All clients in a room share a notion of time. The server's clock is the reference, and each client keeps an estimate of it. On top of that clock the server defines a tick rate, which gives you a fixed-step loop that runs at the same pace everywhere.

docs.title: Server time
docs.text:
Pulse.ServerTime is the estimated server clock in seconds, as a double. Two clients that read it at the same moment get values that differ only by the estimation error, so it is the right time base for things that must line up: countdowns, interpolation, cooldowns that start from a shared event.

How it is estimated: the connection handshake gives a first offset. After that the client sends a ping every two seconds, takes the round-trip time of each answer, keeps the last eight samples and uses the offset of the sample with the lowest round trip. Pulse.RoundTripTimeMs is the transport's round-trip time. Before you connect the value means nothing, and in offline mode it follows the local clock.

A shared countdown is a few lines: the master stores a start time in a room property, and every client computes the remainder from the same clock.

using NetPulse;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class Countdown : MonoBehaviour
{
    private static readonly RoomKey<double> StartAt = new("startAt");

    public void Begin(float seconds) => Pulse.CurrentRoom.Set(StartAt, Pulse.ServerTime + seconds);

    private void Update()
    {
        var room = Pulse.CurrentRoom;
        if (room == null || !room.Properties.ContainsKey(StartAt.Name))
        {
            return;
        }

        var remaining = room.Get(StartAt) - Pulse.ServerTime;
        if (remaining > 0d)
        {
            Debug.Log($"Starting in {remaining:F1} s");
        }
    }
}

Use ServerTime rather than Time.time for anything you compare between clients. NetRpcInfo.ServerTime is the server time on the receiving client when the RPC ran, not when it was sent. To measure travel time, put Pulse.ServerTime into the payload of the message or RPC.

docs.title: Ticks
docs.text:
The server announces a tick rate when you join a room (30 per second unless the server is configured differently). The client uses 30 until then, and in offline mode.

Member Meaning Pulse.TickRate Ticks per second Pulse.Tick The current tick number, floor(ServerTime * TickRate), as a long Pulse.TickDelta The length of one tick in seconds, 1 / TickRate

Because the number comes from the shared clock, every client agrees on which tick is current.

docs.title: OnNetworkTick
docs.text:
Override OnNetworkTick(long tick) in a NetworkBehaviour to run code once per tick. It is called for every spawned object, whether you own it or not, so check IsMine before you act on input.

using NetPulse;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class TickMover : NetworkBehaviour
{
    [SerializeField, Min(0f)] private float _speed = 5f;

    private Vector3 _direction;

    public void SetDirection(Vector3 direction) => _direction = direction;

    public override void OnNetworkTick(long tick)
    {
        if (IsMine)
        {
            transform.position += _direction * (_speed * (float)Pulse.TickDelta);
        }
    }
}

What is guaranteed:

  • OnNetworkSpawned runs before the first OnNetworkTick of an object (lifecycle).
  • Ticks run from the NetPulse runner in Update, before your own Update.
  • If a frame took longer than one tick, the loop catches up, but at most 5 ticks run in one frame. If the application stalled for more than a second, the older ticks are skipped and only the last 5 run.
  • The first frame after joining a room only records the starting tick. The first OnNetworkTick comes in a later frame.
  • An exception in one OnNetworkTick is logged and does not stop the other objects.

docs.title: How ticks drive sending
docs.text:
Object state is sent on tick boundaries, right after the OnNetworkTick calls of that tick, so a change you make in a tick goes out in the same tick. Not every tick sends. The number of ticks between sends comes from two settings (settings and editor):

rate = max(1, min(SendRate, SerializationRate))
ticksPerSend = max(1, round(TickRate / rate))

A SerializationRate of 0 stands for the tick rate in this formula.

Tick rate Send Rate Serialization Rate Sends 30 20 (default) 0 (default) Every 2nd tick, 15 per second 30 30 0 Every tick 30 10 0 Every 3rd tick, 10 per second 30 60 15 Every 2nd tick

The rate applies to all objects. When a player joins, owners resend their full state on the next tick, regardless of the schedule.

docs.title: Interpolation and time
docs.text: Remote objects are shown slightly in the past so that there are always two snapshots to blend. NetworkTransform renders at ServerTime minus a delay. Each snapshot carries the server time of the owner's send, which NetStream.Timestamp exposes if you write your own OnSerialize. See components for the delay setting.

docs.title: NetPulse
docs.text:
NetPulse помогает строить сетевые игры на Unity. Решение состоит из двух частей: сервера на .NET 10, который вы размещаете сами, и Unity-пакета com.netpulse.unity, рассчитанного на Unity от 2021.3 до 6000.x. Если вы работали с Photon PUN, модель вам знакома: игроки подключаются, попадают в лобби, создают комнаты и входят в них, обмениваются свойствами комнаты и игрока, вызывают RPC и синхронизируют сетевые объекты.

Обе части сейчас имеют версию 0.4.

docs.title: Что внутри
docs.text:
Сервер:

  • Лобби и подбор комнат: именованные комнаты, случайный вход с фильтром по свойствам, список комнат с дельтами в реальном времени.
  • Каждая комната работает на своём асинхронном файбере, поэтому медленная комната не задерживает ни другие комнаты, ни лобби, ни сетевой поток.
  • Кэш событий для опоздавших игроков, время жизни игрока и пустой комнаты для повторного входа.
  • Проверка владения сетевыми объектами на сервере: клиент не может двигать, удалять или забирать чужие объекты.
  • Защита от флуда для каждого пира, проверка AppId и версии протокола, необязательная собственная аутентификация.
  • Плагины на C#: хуки входа, событий, изменения свойств и закрытия комнаты, таймеры, HTTP-запросы, фоновая работа и горячая перезагрузка.
  • Метрики через System.Diagnostics.Metrics и небольшой набор консольных команд.

Unity:

  • Асинхронный API (await Pulse.Connect(), await Pulse.JoinOrCreateRoom(...)) с альтернативами на колбэках и корутинах.
  • RPC, SyncVar<T>, типизированные сообщения и типизированные ключи свойств комнаты и игрока. Код для них создаёт генератор исходного кода, а ошибки ловят анализаторы.
  • Сетевые объекты с владением, сценовые объекты, сетевые сцены, сетевой тик и офлайн-режим.
  • Инструменты редактора: ассет настроек, окно Hub с профайлером трафика и генерация link.xml для IL2CPP.

docs.title: Сравнение с PUN
docs.text: Понятия совпадают в основном один в один, поэтому большая часть PUN-кода переносится переименованием. Различия в том, где работает сервер и кто проверяет правила. NetPulse размещается у вас: вы запускаете серверный бинарник на своей машине и пишете серверную логику плагинами на C#, а не пользуетесь облачным сервисом. Владение объектами проверяет сам сервер, а Unity API построен на async/await и сгенерированном коде вместо вызовов по строковым именам. Конкретные замены перечислены на странице Переход с PUN.

docs.title: С чего начать
docs.text:
Если нужно Читайте Запустить сервер и войти в комнату за несколько минут Быстрый старт Понять комнаты, пиры, объекты и владение Основные понятия Написать клиентскую часть Unity-клиент Запустить, настроить и развернуть сервер Сервер Добавить серверную логику Плагины Написать свой клиент или найти код Справочник Перенести проект с PUN Переход с PUN Разобраться с проблемой Решение проблем и Эксплуатация Узнать, что изменилось История изменений

Исходный код обеих частей лежит на GitHub. Пока репозиторий закрытый, поэтому для клонирования сервера и установки Unity-пакета из git нужен доступ к нему.

docs.title: История изменений
docs.text: Изменения сервера, SDK плагинов и общей библиотеки протокола (NetPulse.Common). У Unity-пакета свой список: см. журнал изменений Unity-пакета. Клиенту версии 0.4 нужен сервер версии 0.4.

Шифрование транспорта и усиление сервера. Клиенту 0.4 нужен сервер 0.4. При значении по умолчанию Encryption:Mode = Disabled формат на проводе остаётся таким же, как в 0.3, и клиент 0.3 по-прежнему подключается.

Шифрование:

  • Весь UDP-поток, включая заголовки, подтверждения и сообщения об отключении LiteNetLib, можно шифровать и аутентифицировать. Алгоритмы фиксированы: X25519 с закреплённым ключом сервера через шаблон Noise NK (NKpsk0 с предварительно разделённым ключом), записи ChaCha20-Poly1305 и SHA-256/HKDF. Ничего не согласуется.
  • NetPulse:Encryption: Mode (Disabled, Optional, Required), PrivateKeyFile или NETPULSE_SERVER_PRIVATE_KEY, PreviousPrivateKeyFiles для ротации ключей, PreSharedKey и PreSharedKeyFile, RequireCookie, CookieLifetimeMs, RekeyAfterPackets, RekeyAfterMs, ReplayWindow, SessionIdleTimeoutMs, ReplaceIdleMs, HandshakeTimeoutMs и PaddingBlock. В режиме Optional или Required сервер не запустится без корректного ключа.
  • NetPulse.Server keygen [--out файл] [--force] создаёт файл приватного ключа и печатает публичный.
  • Обмен cookie выполняется до любого обмена ключами, и каждый ответ рукопожатия короче запроса, поэтому сервер нельзя использовать для усиления трафика. Сессию с того же адреса можно заменить только после того, как она промолчала ReplaceIdleMs, причём старый пир отключается первым, так что новая сессия никогда не наследует аутентифицированного пира.
  • NetPulse.Common.Security: управляемые X25519 и ChaCha20-Poly1305 с постоянным временем и без выделений памяти на пути пакета, рукопожатие Noise, cookie, окно повторов, защита записей со сменой ключей, ядра клиента и сервера. Они проверены по векторам RFC 7748, 8439 и 5869 и сравнением с BouncyCastle, BCL и независимой реализацией Noise, только в тестовых проектах.
  • SDK плагинов: AuthRequest.IsEncrypted и AuthRequest.ChannelBinding (32-байтовый хэш рукопожатия), IActor.IsEncrypted.
  • Метрики netpulse.handshakes_ok, handshakes_failed, handshakes_rate_limited, cookies_sent, decrypt_failures, replays, rekeys и plaintext_rejected.
  • NetPulse.TestClient умеет шифровать: --encrypt --server-public-key КЛЮЧ [--psk КЛЮЧ] [--padding N].

Лимиты (NetPulse:Security, 0 выключает лимит):

  • На адрес: MaxConnectionsPerIp, ConnectionAttemptsPerIpPerSecond, HandshakesPerIpPerSecond; на весь сервер MaxHandshakesPerSecond. Они работают и без шифрования там, где применимы.
  • На пира: AuthDeadlineMs, MaxAuthAttempts, token bucket MaxMessagesPerSecond/MessageBurst и MaxBytesPerSecond/ByteBurst, а также MaxMessageBytes. Нарушение отключает пира с причиной RateLimited, AuthTimeout или TooManyAuthAttempts.
  • Размеры: MaxUserIdLength, MaxNickNameLength, MaxAuthTokenLength, MaxRoomNameLength, MaxPropertiesPerRoom, MaxPropertyBytes, MaxCachedEventsPerRoom, MaxTargetActors. Запрос сверх лимита отклоняется с InvalidRequest, а не обрезается. Управляющие символы в идентификаторах пользователей, никнеймах и именах комнат отклоняются, а в тексте для лога заменяются.
  • RequireRejoinToken: сервер выдаёт случайный токен при каждом входе и требует его, когда возвращается неактивный игрок, так что другой клиент с тем же UserId место не займёт. Новое поле протокола RejoinToken (ParamKey 56).
  • NetReader отказывается читать больше 4096 вложенных контейнеров в одном сообщении.
  • Новые метрики netpulse.peers_rate_limited, connections_rejected, auth_timeouts и limit_violations.

Исправления:

  • Клиент, вошедший в лобби, мог сразу после полного списка получить устаревшую дельту списка комнат. Теперь лобби рассылает накопленные дельты, прежде чем добавить подписчика.

Тесты: всего 292, из них 112 для Common, 34 для генераторов и 146 для сервера. Новые тесты включают сквозные прогоны по реальному UDP в режимах Disabled, Optional и Required через записывающий прокси с повторёнными, изменёнными, удержанными и потерянными датаграммами.

Поддержка облегчённого Unity API и генератора исходного кода.

Протокол и NetPulse.Common:

  • Новый код типа значения Extended (18) с NetTypeRegistry.RegisterExtended, IsExtendedRegistered и UnregisterExtended. Расширенное значение несёт идентификатор ushort и длину. Сервер или клиент, не знающий идентификатор, сохраняет значение как OpaqueValue и пересылает без изменений.
  • В NetWriter и NetReader добавлены методы для sbyte, ulong и char.
  • Новые события: Message (244) для типизированных сообщений и SyncVarSet (245) для sync-переменных мастера.
  • Новое зарезервированное свойство комнаты _scene и RoomPropertyKeys.Scene.
  • RaiseEventRequest.ObjectFlags с флагом PersistAcrossScenes.
  • Ответ на вход содержит TickRate.

Сервер:

  • SyncVarSet и изменения _scene принимаются только от мастер-клиента.
  • Смена сцены удаляет сценовые объекты и объекты, не помеченные как постоянные, вместе с их кэшированными событиями.
  • NetPulse:TickRate теперь отправляется и клиентам, которые используют его для сетевого тика.

SDK плагинов:

  • INetworkObject.IsPersistent.

Инструменты и тесты:

  • NetPulse.Unity.Generators: генератор исходного кода Roslyn и анализаторы от NP0001 до NP0011 для Unity-пакета, а также tools/build-generators.ps1 для копирования собранной dll в пакет.
  • 159 тестов: 41 для Common, 34 для генераторов и 84 для сервера.

Первая версия в истории git.

  • Асинхронные комнаты: каждая комната работает на своём файбере, который дожидается каждого элемента очереди, поэтому медленная комната не задерживает ни другие комнаты, ни лобби, ни сетевой поток.
  • Хуки плагинов асинхронные (ValueTask с CancellationToken) и имеют тайм-аут (NetPulse:Plugins:HookTimeoutMs). Синхронные хуки и Defer() удалены. Хук, завершившийся без решения, считается Fail.
  • API хоста: асинхронные таймеры на PeriodicTimer, Enqueue, HttpAsync и RunInBackground.
  • Защита от флуда для каждого пира (PeerQueueLimit) с границей очереди каждой комнаты (RoomQueueCapacity) и причиной отключения Overloaded.
  • Проверка владения сетевыми объектами на сервере с тремя режимами (Fixed, Takeover, Request), операциями RequestOwnership и RegisterSceneObjects и событием OwnershipRequested. Хук OnBeforeTransferOwnershipAsync позволяет плагинам накладывать вето на передачу.
  • Собственная аутентификация через IAuthPlugin с AuthTimeoutMs и сервер, который отказывается запускаться, если настроенный плагин аутентификации не загрузился. Плагин AuthSample имеет режимы HMAC и HTTP, а тестовый клиент умеет создавать токены командой --make-token.
  • Горячая перезагрузка плагинов с изолированными контекстами загрузки и консольная команда reload.
  • Лобби с дельтами списка комнат, случайный вход с фильтрами по свойствам, время жизни игрока и пустой комнаты, обновление свойств через сравнение и замену (CAS), группы интереса и кэш событий.
  • Метрики под метром NetPulse и консольные команды stats, plugins, reload и quit.
  • NetPulse.TestClient, клиент-бот для проверок.
Первоначальный протокол, NetPulse.Common, лобби и комнаты и первые хуки плагинов. Эта версия появилась до истории git.

docs.title: Основные понятия
docs.text: На этой странице собраны термины, которые используются во всех остальных разделах: что хранит сервер, кто что может менять и какая возможность NetPulse подходит для какой задачи. Прочитайте её один раз перед практическими страницами.

docs.title: Общая картина
docs.text:
Игровой клиент подключается к одному серверу NetPulse по надёжному UDP. Клиент представляется через AppId и AppVersion, а сервер принимает его или отклоняет. После подключения клиент может зайти в лобби, создать комнату или войти в существующую и играть. Всё, что происходит во время игры, относится к одной комнате.

Сервер пересылает сообщения и следит за несколькими правилами: владение объектами, кто может менять сцену, кто может писать master-переменные. Код вашей игры на сервере не выполняется. Игровая логика живёт в клиентах, а проверки и серверную авторитетность при желании добавляют плагины. См. обзор сервера и быстрый старт.

Клиент целиком работает в главном потоке Unity. Фоновых колбэков нет, поэтому из любого события NetPulse и из продолжения после await можно свободно обращаться к объектам Unity.

docs.title: Состояния подключения
docs.text:
Pulse.State проходит через такие значения:

Состояние Значение Disconnected Нет соединения. Начальное и конечное состояние. Connecting Идёт UDP-рукопожатие. Authenticating Соединение с сервером есть, идёт проверка AppId и токена. Connected Можно входить в лобби или в комнату. InLobby Клиент получает актуальный список комнат. JoiningRoom Запрос на создание или вход ещё выполняется. InRoom Клиент в комнате. Объекты, RPC и сообщения работают только здесь. Leaving Запрос на выход ещё выполняется.

В NetState есть и значение Disconnecting, но текущий клиент в него не переходит. Подробности на странице подключения.

docs.title: Лобби и комнаты
docs.text:
Единица игры здесь комната. У неё есть имя, максимум игроков (0 означает без ограничения), флаг открытости (можно ли входить) и флаг видимости (показывать ли в списке комнат), а также пользовательские свойства, доступные всем участникам. Когда последний игрок выходит, комната закрывается, если только в настройках комнаты не задано держать её ещё какое-то время.

Лобби необязательно: это каталог видимых комнат. После входа в лобби вы получаете список, который сервер поддерживает актуальным. Чтобы войти в комнату по имени или в случайную комнату, лобби не нужно. См. подбор комнат.

docs.title: Игроки, ActorId и UserId
docs.text:
У каждого игрока в комнате три идентификатора:

  • ActorId сервер назначает при входе игрока в комнату. В каждой новой комнате счёт начинается с 1 и растёт. Один и тот же номер в комнате не выдаётся дважды. Используйте его, чтобы ссылаться на игрока внутри комнаты.
  • UserId идентифицирует человека между сессиями. Клиент генерирует его сам и хранит в PlayerPrefs, если не выключен Persist User Id. Плагин аутентификации может его заменить. Игрок, который отключился и вернулся с тем же UserId, может занять прежнее место с прежним ActorId, если комната хранит неактивных игроков.
  • NickName служит отображаемым именем. Уникальность не гарантируется.

Локальный игрок доступен как Pulse.LocalPlayer. Игрок может быть неактивным: он вышел через LeaveRoom(true) или потерял соединение, а комната на ограниченное время сохраняет его место. См. подбор комнат.

docs.title: Мастер-клиент
docs.text:
В каждой комнате один из игроков мастер-клиент. Сервер выбирает активного игрока, который находится в комнате дольше всех, и выбирает заново, когда тот уходит. Все клиенты получают уведомление о смене.

Мастер-клиент остаётся обычным клиентом, но с обязанностями, встроенными в NetPulse:

  • Только мастер может загрузить сетевую сцену (сцены).
  • Только мастер может менять переменные Master (синхронизация состояния).
  • Сценовые объекты принадлежат мастеру (сетевые объекты).
  • RpcTarget.MasterClient доставляет вызов ему.

Поскольку это клиент, относитесь к мастеру как к удобству, а не как к доверенной стороне. Сервер проверяет владение и правила «только для мастера», а плагины могут проверять больше.

docs.title: События, получатели и кэширование
docs.text:
Всё, что клиент отправляет в комнату, на нижнем уровне является событием: RPC, типизированное сообщение, создание объекта, обновление состояния. У события есть код, данные, набор получателей, режим доставки, необязательная группа интереса и необязательный режим кэширования.

  • Получатели: все остальные (Others), все включая отправителя (All), только мастер-клиент или список конкретных акторов.
  • Доставка: ReliableOrdered, ReliableUnordered, UnreliableSequenced или Unreliable. Надёжные режимы повторяют отправку, ненадёжные нет.
  • Кэширование: событие можно сохранить в кэше комнаты. Сервер проигрывает кэш каждому, кто войдёт позже, и именно так опоздавшие видят объекты, созданные до их прихода. Буферизованные RPC и создание объектов используют кэш.

Коды от 0 до 199 свободны для ваших событий. Коды от 230 до 250 зарезервированы под систему. В большинстве случаев работать с кодами событий не нужно: RPC и сообщения скрывают их. О Pulse.RaiseEvent рассказывает страница низкоуровневого API.

docs.title: Сетевые объекты и ViewId
docs.text:
Сетевой объект представляет собой GameObject с компонентом NetworkObject. У каждого есть ViewId, целое число, одинаковое на всех клиентах и однозначно называющее объект в комнате.

  • Объекты, созданные через Pulse.Instantiate, получают ViewId вида ActorId * 1000 + n. Так актор с номером 2 создаёт объекты 2001, 2002 и далее, а каждый игрок может одновременно иметь до 999 живых объектов.
  • Сценовые объекты (расставленные в сцене в редакторе) используют свой Scene Id от 1 до 999 как view id.

У каждого сетевого объекта один владелец. Только владелец отправляет состояние объекта, и только у него IsMine равно true. Остальные клиенты получают состояние и применяют его. Каждый NetworkBehaviour на объекте (корень и его потомки) адресуется по индексу, поэтому иерархия должна совпадать на всех клиентах. См. сетевые объекты.

docs.title: Режимы владения
docs.text:
У каждого объекта есть режим владения. Он задаётся на NetworkObject и отправляется на сервер при создании объекта:

Режим Кто может стать владельцем Fixed Никто. Объект остаётся у создателя. Takeover Любой, сразу, по запросу. Request Любой, но текущий владелец должен одобрить.

Сервер проверяет каждую смену владельца и каждое обновление состояния, поэтому клиент не может писать в чужой объект. Когда игрок уходит, объекты, которыми он владел в этот момент, уничтожаются, кроме сценовых: они возвращаются мастеру. См. владение.

docs.title: Состояние, RPC, сообщения и свойства
docs.text:
NetPulse предлагает несколько способов передавать данные. Выбирайте по форме данных:

Вам нужно Используйте Хранить данные всей комнаты, которые получат и опоздавшие (карта, номер раунда, счёт) Свойства комнаты, обычно с типизированным RoomKey<T> (комнаты и свойства) Хранить данные игрока, которые видят остальные (команда, флаг готовности) Свойства игрока, через PlayerKey<T> Сообщить комнате о чём-то, не привязанном к объекту (чат, событие матча) Типизированное сообщение (сообщения) Заставить что-то произойти на конкретном объекте у других клиентов (выстрел, попадание, открытие двери) RPC (RPC) Держать в синхронизации одно значение объекта (здоровье, цвет, счёт) SyncVar<T> (синхронизация состояния) Передавать поток своих, часто меняющихся данных объекта Поля [Synced] или OnSerialize Двигать трансформ, rigidbody или аниматор Готовые компоненты (компоненты)

Практическое правило: свойства хранят данные, которые помнит комната, RPC и сообщения описывают разовые события, а SyncVar и синхронизация состояния удерживают значения одинаковыми у всех клиентов.

docs.title: Серверное время и тики
docs.text:
У сервера есть часы. Клиент оценивает смещение относительно них по рукопожатию и по пингу, который отправляется каждые две секунды, и выдаёт результат как Pulse.ServerTime в секундах. Все клиенты видят почти одно и то же значение, поэтому оно подходит как основа для интерполяции и для всего, что должно совпадать по времени.

Сервер также объявляет частоту тиков (по умолчанию 30). Тик представляет собой пронумерованный отрезок серверного времени: Pulse.Tick равен floor(ServerTime * TickRate). NetworkBehaviour.OnNetworkTick вызывается один раз за тик, а состояние отправляется на границах тиков. См. тики и время.

docs.title: Группы интереса
docs.text:
Группа интереса ограничивает круг получателей события. Группа 0 означает всех. Событие, отправленное в группу 5, получат только игроки, подписавшиеся на группу 5 через Pulse.ChangeInterestGroups. Группу можно задать сетевому объекту, чтобы весь его трафик фильтровался; так делят карту на зоны, команды или уровни детализации. См. низкоуровневый API.

Есть два ограничения. События для мастер-клиента или для списка конкретных акторов группу игнорируют. А кэш комнаты проигрывается один раз, при входе игрока, поэтому подписка на группу позже не доставит задним числом кэшированные события этой группы.

docs.title: Быстрый старт
docs.text: Эта страница ведёт от пустого проекта к Unity-клиенту, который сидит в комнате на вашем собственном сервере. Каждый шаг ссылается на подробные страницы.

docs.title: Что понадобится
docs.text:
• .NET 10 SDK, чтобы собрать и запустить сервер.
  • Unity 2021.3 или новее (6000.x тоже подходит) для клиента.
  • Доступ по git к репозиториям NetPulse. Пока они закрытые.

docs.title: 1. Запустите сервер
docs.text:
Клонируйте репозиторий сервера, соберите и запустите его:

git clone https://github.com/Klobiroff/NetPulse-Server.git
cd NetPulse-Server
dotnet build
dotnet run --project src/NetPulse.Server

Сборка заодно копирует пример плагина в папку plugins сервера. Сервер пишет в лог порт, который он слушает:

info: NetPulse.Server.Plugins.PluginManager[0] Loaded plugin NetPulse.Plugins.Sample v1 from NetPulse.Plugins.Sample
info: NetPulse.Server.Networking.NetPulseServer[0] NetPulse server listening on UDP 5055
info: NetPulse.Server.Commands.ConsoleCommandService[0] Console commands: stats, plugins, reload <folder>, quit

Порт по умолчанию: UDP 5055. Если между сервером и клиентами стоит файрвол, откройте этот UDP-порт. Подробности в разделе Запуск сервера.

Чтобы проверить сервер, не открывая Unity, запустите двух тестовых ботов во втором терминале:

dotnet run --project tools/NetPulse.TestClient -- --bots 2 --room test --seconds 6

Боты входят в комнату test, обмениваются событиями и в конце печатают OK, если всё прошло успешно.

docs.title: 2. Установите Unity-пакет
docs.text:
Пакет лежит в репозитории Unity в папке Packages/com.netpulse.unity. Откройте Window > Package Manager, нажмите +, выберите Add package from git URL и вставьте:

https://github.com/Klobiroff/NetPulse-Unity.git?path=Packages/com.netpulse.unity

Git запускает сам Unity, поэтому на машине должен быть установлен git, а также учётные данные с правом чтения закрытого репозитория.

Нет доступа к git?

Скопируйте папку Packages/com.netpulse.unity из клона репозитория Unity в папку Packages вашего проекта. Unity подхватит её при следующей перезагрузке доменов. Можно также выбрать Add package from disk и указать package.json внутри этой папки.

Подробнее на странице Установка.

docs.title: 3. Настройте подключение
docs.text: Откройте Project Settings > NetPulse (или NetPulse > Create Settings Asset). Unity создаст Assets/Resources/NetPulseSettings.asset. Укажите хост и порт сервера. Оставьте AppId пустым, если не задавали NetPulse:AppId на сервере. См. Настройки и редактор.

docs.title: 4. Подключитесь и войдите в комнату
docs.text:
Добавьте этот скрипт на любой GameObject в сцене:

using NetPulse;
using NetPulse.Common;
using UnityEngine;

public sealed class Demo : MonoBehaviour
{
    private async void Start()
    {
        Pulse.NickName = "Alice";
        await Pulse.Connect();
        var room = await Pulse.JoinOrCreateRoom("arena", new RoomOptions { MaxPlayers = 4 });
        Debug.Log($"Joined {room.Name}, players: {room.PlayerCount}");
    }
}

Нажмите Play. В логе сервера для первого игрока появится строка Creating room arena for .... Запустите вторую копию (сборку или экземпляр Multiplayer Play Mode), и число игроков вырастет.

Неудавшаяся операция бросает NetPulseException с ReturnCode от сервера. Коды перечислены в Коды и ключи.

docs.title: Что читать дальше
docs.text:
• Основные понятия объясняют комнаты, пиры, сетевые объекты и владение.
  • Подключение и Подбор комнат описывают лобби и разные способы входа.
  • Сетевые объекты и RPC отвечают за синхронизацию геймплея.
  • Конфигурация перечисляет все настройки сервера, а Написание плагина показывает, как добавить серверную логику.

docs.title: Переход с PUN
docs.text: Если вы знаете Photon PUN 2, большая часть NetPulse покажется знакомой: комнаты, мастер-клиент, NetworkObject в роли PhotonView, [NetRpc] в роли [PunRPC], режимы владения, пользовательские свойства. На этой странице сопоставлены понятия и API, которые в NetPulse действительно есть, а затем перечислены отличия.

docs.title: Подключение и комнаты
docs.text: PUN 2 NetPulse PhotonNetwork.ConnectUsingSettings() Pulse.Connect(); настройки лежат в NetPulseSettings PhotonServerSettings (AppId, регион) NetPulseSettings (хост, порт, AppId, AppVersion) PhotonNetwork.GameVersion AppVersion в настройках PhotonNetwork.NickName Pulse.NickName PhotonNetwork.AuthValues Pulse.AuthToken, проверяется серверным плагином аутентификации PhotonNetwork.NetworkClientState Pulse.State (NetState) PhotonNetwork.IsConnected, InRoom Pulse.IsConnected, Pulse.IsInRoom PhotonNetwork.GetPing() Pulse.RoundTripTimeMs PhotonNetwork.Disconnect() Pulse.Disconnect() PhotonNetwork.OfflineMode Pulse.OfflineMode PhotonNetwork.JoinLobby(), LeaveLobby() Pulse.JoinLobby(), Pulse.LeaveLobby() OnRoomListUpdate(List<RoomInfo>) (только изменения) OnRoomListUpdate(IReadOnlyList<RoomInfo>), всегда полный объединённый список; также Pulse.LobbyRooms, Pulse.GetRoomList() PhotonNetwork.CreateRoom(name, options) Pulse.CreateRoom(name, options) PhotonNetwork.JoinRoom(name) Pulse.JoinRoom(name) PhotonNetwork.JoinOrCreateRoom(name, options, lobby) Pulse.JoinOrCreateRoom(name, options) PhotonNetwork.JoinRandomRoom(props, maxPlayers) Pulse.JoinRandomRoom(expectedProperties, expectedMaxPlayers, createOptions); может создать комнату, если ничего не подошло PhotonNetwork.LeaveRoom(becomeInactive) Pulse.LeaveRoom(becomeInactive) RoomOptions.MaxPlayers, IsVisible, IsOpen Те же имена в RoomOptions RoomOptions.CustomRoomProperties RoomOptions.CustomProperties RoomOptions.CustomRoomPropertiesForLobby RoomOptions.LobbyProperties RoomOptions.PlayerTtl, EmptyRoomTtl RoomOptions.PlayerTtlMs, EmptyRoomTtlMs PhotonNetwork.CurrentRoom, LocalPlayer, IsMasterClient Pulse.CurrentRoom, Pulse.LocalPlayer, Pulse.IsMasterClient PhotonNetwork.PlayerList Pulse.CurrentRoom.Players PhotonNetwork.MasterClient Pulse.CurrentRoom.MasterClient PhotonNetwork.Time Pulse.ServerTime, в секундах типа double PhotonNetwork.SendRate, SerializationRate Поля с теми же именами в NetPulseSettings PhotonNetwork.LoadLevel(scene) с AutomaticallySyncScene Pulse.LoadScene(scene) с Auto Sync Scene, только мастер

docs.title: Игроки и свойства
docs.text: PUN 2 NetPulse Player.ActorNumber Player.ActorId Player.NickName, UserId, IsLocal, IsMasterClient, IsInactive Те же имена Пользовательские свойства Hashtable PropertyTable; player.SetProperty(key, value), GetProperty<T>(key) SetCustomProperties(props, expectedProps) SetProperties(delta, expected) (compare-and-set); типизированные RoomKey<T> и PlayerKey<T> с Set, Get, SetAsync OnRoomPropertiesUpdate(Hashtable) OnRoomPropertiesChanged(PropertyTable), room.OnChanged(key, handler) OnPlayerPropertiesUpdate(Player, Hashtable) OnPlayerPropertiesChanged(Player, PropertyTable), player.OnChanged(key, handler) Room.IsOpen = false room.SetProperty("_isOpen", false), только мастер

docs.title: Объекты, RPC и состояние
docs.text:
PUN 2 NetPulse PhotonView NetworkObject MonoBehaviourPun, photonView.IsMine NetworkBehaviour, IsMine photonView.ViewID, PhotonView.Find(id) NetworkObject.ViewId, Pulse.FindObject(viewId) photonView.Owner, OwnerActorNr Owner, OwnerActorId PhotonNetwork.Instantiate("PrefabName", ...) из Resources Pulse.Instantiate(prefab, ...) с NetworkPrefabRegistry; перегрузка по имени тоже есть photonView.InstantiationData (object[]) NetworkObject.InstantiationData (один object) IPunInstantiateMagicCallback.OnPhotonInstantiate OnNetworkSpawned() PhotonNetwork.Destroy(go) Pulse.Destroy(go) [PunRPC] и photonView.RPC("Name", RpcTarget.All, args) [NetRpc] и Rpc.Name(args) или Rpc.To(RpcTarget.All).Name(args); строковая форма: CallRpc(nameof(Name), RpcTarget.All, args) RpcTarget.All, Others, MasterClient, AllBuffered, OthersBuffered Те же имена. RpcTarget.Owner новый. Вариантов ...ViaServer нет. PhotonMessageInfo NetRpcInfo (Sender, SenderActorId, ServerTime) IPunObservable.OnPhotonSerializeView(stream, info) OnSerialize(NetStream stream) stream.IsWriting, SendNext, ReceiveNext() То же, с ReceiveNext<T>(); либо stream.Serialize(ref value) для обоих направлений Добавление скрипта в Observed Components Не нужно. Синхронизируется любой NetworkBehaviour, который переопределяет OnSerialize или содержит SyncVar.
